definition_zh: 察觉；发现；检测
definition_en: to notice or find something that is not easy to see
core_image: 黑暗里一支手电扫过地面，照出一小片被踩乱的草
scene: 仪器在空气里筛了很久，终于亮起一盏小灯。 The device can detect a gas leak within seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 detect 指「检测出」（第 2 个义项：用仪器或检验方法发现某物）；句意是这台装置能在几秒内检测出气体泄漏。

senses.title: Notice what is barely there
senses.definition: to notice something small or hidden that is not obvious
senses.definitionCN: 注意到不明显的小事或隐藏的事物
senses.example: He detected a slight change in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他察觉到她声音里有一点变化。
senses.why: The senses work below the level of attention and report a difference.
senses.whyCN: 感官在注意力之下工作，然后报告出一处不同。

senses.title: Find it with an instrument
senses.definition: to discover something by using a device or a test
senses.definitionCN: 借助装置或检验方法发现某物
senses.example: The device can detect a gas leak within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这台装置能在几秒内检测出气体泄漏。
senses.why: A machine can extend the senses into places a body cannot go.
senses.whyCN: 机器能把感官延伸到身体去不了的地方。

senses.title: Find it out after searching
senses.definition: to find out something hidden after careful looking or investigation
senses.definitionCN: 经过仔细查找或调查后发现隐藏的事
senses.example: Investigators detected a pattern in the thefts.
senses.exampleCN: 调查人员在这些盗窃案中查出了一个规律。
senses.why: Pieces that look separate become a pattern once someone compares them.
senses.whyCN: 看起来互不相干的碎片，一旦有人对照，就成了规律。

intro.en: Detect comes from Latin detegere, to uncover, built on de-, un-, and tegere, to cover.
intro.cn: detect 来自拉丁语 detegere（揭开），由 de-（去除）与 tegere（覆盖）构成。

items.en: Tegere meant to cover, as a roof covers a house.
items.cn: tegere 指覆盖，就像屋顶盖住房子。

items.en: Detegere meant to take the cover off and bring something to light.
items.cn: detegere 指把覆盖物拿走，让某物露出来。

items.en: Detectus described a thing laid bare.
items.cn: detectus 形容一件被摊开在光下的东西。

items.en: English used detect for uncovering a crime or a secret.
items.cn: 英语用 detect 表示揭出罪行或秘密。

items.en: Instruments gave the word its scientific sense of measuring faint signals.
items.cn: 仪器给了这个词测量微弱信号的科学含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tect shape, and the meaning group all describe becoming aware of something hidden.
note.cn: 形近组共用 tect 这一形状，近义组则都表示察觉到隐藏的事物。

entries.definition: a person who solves crimes
entries.definitionCN: 侦破案件的人

entries.definition: the act of finding something hidden
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏事物的行为

entries.definition: a device that finds something
entries.definitionCN: 用来发现某物的装置

entries.definition: to become aware of something
entries.definitionCN: 意识到某事物的存在

entries.definition: to find something for the first time
entries.definitionCN: 第一次找到某物

entries.definition: to see something suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 突然看见某物

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a torch beam on trampled grass and end with a pattern inside a pile of reports.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从黑暗中扫过草地的手电光开始，落到一叠报告里的规律。

normal.en: To detect is to take the cover off something that wanted to stay hidden.
normal.cn: 察觉就是把某样想藏起来的东西揭开盖。

normal.en: De- plus tegere: the roof comes off and the thing is seen.
normal.cn: de- 加 tegere：屋顶被掀开，东西就露出来了。

normal.en: A good ear detects what a loud room hides.
normal.cn: 好耳朵能听出吵闹房间藏起来的东西。

normal.en: A machine detects signals too faint for a hand to feel.
normal.cn: 机器能检测出手都感觉不到的微弱信号。

normal.en: Detectives detect patterns, not just single events.
normal.cn: 侦探查的是规律，不只是单个事件。

abstract.en: Picture a beam of light stopping on bent grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光停在压弯的草上。

abstract.en: Picture a small light turning red in a silent room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静房间里一盏小灯转红。

abstract.en: Picture three reports laid side by side with one number repeated.
abstract.cn: 想象三份报告并排摊开，同一个数字反复出现。

examples.en: He detected a slight change in her voice.
examples.cn: 他察觉到她声音里有一点变化。

examples.en: The device can detect a gas leak within seconds.
examples.cn: 这台装置能在几秒内检测出气体泄漏。

examples.en: Investigators detected a pattern in the thefts.
examples.cn: 调查人员在这些盗窃案中查出了一个规律。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 detect 记成「地太克特」：de 是去掉，tect 是盖子，把盖子去掉，就察觉到了。

root: 来自拉丁语 detegere，由 de-（去除）与 tegere（覆盖）组成，本义是揭开覆盖物、使东西露出来。后来指发现隐藏的罪行与秘密，现代又指用仪器测出肉眼看不见的微弱信号。

sensesIntro.en: From a cover lifted off, to a faint signal caught by a machine, to a pattern found in scattered facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被揭开的盖子，到机器捕捉到的微弱信号，再到零散事实里找出的规律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cover lifted so that something shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖子被掀开，某样东西露出来。

branches.en: The first sense is a small difference caught by the senses.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是感官捉住的一处细小不同。

branches.en: The second sense is a device doing the catching.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是由装置来完成这次捕捉。

branches.en: The third sense is a pattern assembled from many catches.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是用许多次捕捉拼出的规律。

branches.en: Ears and meters both work by noticing a difference.
branches.cn: 耳朵与仪表，都靠注意到一处不同来工作。

branches.en: One reading detects a leak; many readings detect a habit.
branches.cn: 一次读数检测出泄漏，许多次读数检测出一种习惯。

intro.en: Detect forms a family about uncovering, from the person who looks to the device that measures.
intro.cn: detect 长出一族表示揭开的词，从负责查找的人到负责测量的装置。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin tegere, to cover, and de- takes the cover away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 tegere（覆盖），前缀 de- 把覆盖物拿走。

items.example: They detected smoke in the hall.
They spent the day detecting leaks.
items.exampleCN: 他们花了一天检测泄漏。

items.example: The error went undetected for years.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误多年未被发现。

definition_zh: 生产；产量；制作；（作品的）上演；生成
definition_en: the process of making goods, or the amount made
core_image: 一条流水线把原料一路推成成品，末端的成品箱不断堆高
scene: 工厂把旧线改成两班倒之后，一个月的成品数量翻了一倍。 After the second shift was added, monthly production doubled.
sceneCN: 工厂把旧线改成两班倒，一个月的成品数量翻了一倍；句中的 production 指「把原料制成成品的过程及其产出」（第 1 个义项：制造商品的活动）。图中可辨识物件：流水线、成品箱、排班表、计数器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 生产；产量；制作；上演；生成

senses.title: The making of goods
senses.definition: the activity of making goods from materials, especially in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 用材料制造商品的活动，尤指大量制造
senses.example: After the second shift was added, monthly production doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 加上第二班之后，月产量翻了一倍。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to lead forward, so the word begins as bringing something out into being.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前引出」，因此这个词起于「把东西带出来、造出来」。

senses.title: The amount produced
senses.definition: the total quantity of something made in a given period
senses.definitionCN: 某段时期内造出的总量
senses.example: Rice production reached a ten-year high.
senses.exampleCN: 稻米产量达到十年来的最高点。
senses.why: The noun of the process slides into naming its result, so production can be a number.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词滑向指结果，因此 production 可以是一个数字。

senses.title: Economic output of goods and services
senses.titleCN: 经济意义上的商品与服务产出
senses.definition: the creation of goods and services measured as a whole economy's activity
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体经济活动衡量的商品与服务创造
senses.example: The region's production grew faster than its population.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的产出增长快于人口增长。
senses.why: Economics treats the whole making activity as one quantity, which is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把全部制造活动当作一个量，这就是此义。

senses.title: Staging a play or film
senses.titleCN: 戏剧或影视的排演制作
senses.definition: the work of preparing and presenting a play, film or programme
senses.definitionCN: 筹备并呈现戏剧、电影或节目的工作
senses.example: Production on the film took fourteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的制作花了十四个月。
senses.why: A play is brought out before an audience, which is the same leading-forward image in culture.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧被带到观众面前，与文化领域的「引出」意象相同。

senses.title: Bringing forth knowledge or results
senses.definition: the act of generating ideas, evidence or results rather than goods
senses.definitionCN: 产生想法、证据或成果而非货物的行为
senses.example: The lab's production of reliable data made the review possible.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室产出可靠数据，才使这次评审成为可能。
senses.why: Anything brought into existence can be produced, so the word extends from factories to research.
senses.whyCN: 任何被带进存在的东西都可被「生产」，因此这个词从工厂延伸到研究。

senses.title: A bodily substance generated
senses.definition: the generation of a substance by a living body, such as a hormone
senses.definitionCN: 活体生成某种物质，如激素
senses.example: Stress increases the production of cortisol.
senses.exampleCN: 压力会增加皮质醇的生成。
senses.why: Biology keeps the core meaning of bringing something forth, with no factory involved.
senses.whyCN: 生物学保留「带出某物」的核心义，却不涉及工厂。

senses.title: The stage of being made
senses.definition: the stage at which something is being manufactured or filmed
senses.definitionCN: 某物正在被制造或拍摄的阶段
senses.example: The new model is in production but not yet on sale.
senses.exampleCN: 新车型已在生产，但尚未开售。
senses.why: The phrase in production names a phase of the process, which is why it takes a fixed preposition.
senses.whyCN: in production 指过程的一个阶段，因此配固定介词。

senses.title: A particular staged work
senses.definition: a single play, film or show as staged by a company
senses.definitionCN: 某团体排演的一部戏、电影或节目
senses.example: The festival opened with a new production of the opera.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术节以这部歌剧的新制作开幕。
senses.why: The process noun finally stands for one finished work, a countable product of the stage.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词最终指一部成品，成为舞台上可数的产物。

intro.en: Production comes from Latin productio, 'a bringing forth', from producere 'to lead forward', built on pro- 'forward' and ducere 'to lead'. English took it through French in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: production 来自拉丁 productio「带出、引出」，源自动词 producere「向前引出」，由 pro-「向前」与 ducere「引导」构成，十五世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. It gives duct, conduct, introduce, reduce and educate.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，衍生 duct、conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere produced producere, 'to lead or bring forward, to bring out'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 构成 producere，意为「向前引出、带出」。

items.en: Productio named a bringing forth or a stretching out; the sense of making goods grew later.
items.cn: productio 指「带出、拉长」；制造货物的意思出现较晚。

items.en: English adopted production through French, at first for bringing something into existence rather than for factories.
items.cn: 英语经法语吸收 production，最初指使某物产生，而非工厂制造。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century industry fixed the modern sense: the making of goods in quantity, measured as output.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的工业固定了现代义：大量制造货物，并以产出计量。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether the noun came directly from Latin or through French is not settled, and the earliest date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个名词是直接来自拉丁语还是经法语传入，尚无定论；最早年代也是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same lead-forward root that are easily confused; group two holds near words for making and output.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「向前引出」词根、易混的词；第二组是表示制造与产出的近义词。

entries.definition: Same root: the thing that results, while production is the activity or the total amount.
entries.definitionCN: 同根：指产生的那件东西，而 production 指活动或总量。

entries.definition: The verb of making, and as a noun farm goods; it is the action behind production.
entries.definitionCN: 表示制造的动词，作名词时指农产品；是 production 背后的动作。

entries.definition: The one who makes, or the one who organizes a film; it names an agent, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 制造者或组织影片的人；指施动者而非过程。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus production: the making of a copy, or the biological bearing of young.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再」加 production：复制，或生物的繁殖。

entries.definition: What comes out of a process, especially as a measured quantity; it matches sense two closely.
entries.definitionCN: 一个过程的产物，尤指可计量的数量；与第 2 义接近。

entries.definition: Making goods on an industrial scale; it stresses factories and hands, where production is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 工业规模地制造货物；强调工厂与手工，而 production 范围更广。

entries.definition: The producing of something, especially energy or offspring; it is closer to the older sense than to factory output.
entries.definitionCN: 产生某物，尤指能源或后代；比工厂产出更接近较早的词义。

entries.definition: Bringing something into existence, often artistic or original; production may only repeat an existing design.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物产生，常指艺术或原创；production 可能只是重复既有设计。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the lead-forward root, the fixed phrases and the industrial sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「向前引出」词根、固定搭配与工业义。

normal.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'lead': production leads material forward into a product.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」：生产把材料一路引成产品。

normal.en: The family runs produce, producer, product, productive, productivity and reproduction.
normal.cn: 同族词有 produce、producer、product、productive、productivity 与 reproduction。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: production line, mass production, production costs, in production.
normal.cn: 固定说法：生产线、批量生产、生产成本、在生产中。

normal.en: The same root appears in conduct, introduce, reduce and educate.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate 中。

normal.en: Economics pairs it with consumption: what is made and what is used up.
normal.cn: 经济学把它与消费配对：造出来的与用掉的。

abstract.en: Picture raw bales entering one end of a line and boxes leaving the other.
abstract.cn: 想象原料包从流水线一端进去，成品箱从另一端出来。

abstract.en: Picture a counter that clicks once per finished item all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只计数器，每出一件成品就跳一下，整天不停。

abstract.en: Picture a stage where a script slowly becomes a lit set.
abstract.cn: 想象一方舞台，剧本慢慢变成亮起的布景。

examples.en: The factory raised production without adding a single worker.
examples.cn: 工厂没有增加一名工人就提高了产量。

examples.en: Steel production fell during the third quarter.
examples.cn: 第三季度钢铁产量下降。

examples.en: The new production of the play moved the action to a modern city.
examples.cn: 这部戏的新制作把故事搬到了现代城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ duct（引导）+ ion」——把原料一路引出来，就是生产

root: 拉丁 productio「带出、引出」，来自 producere = pro-（向前）+ ducere「引导」；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bringing-forth: making goods, the amount made, the whole economy's output, a staged work, new knowledge, a bodily substance, the stage of being made and finally one finished production.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「带出」这个动作：制造货物、产量、整体经济产出、舞台制作、新知识、体内物质、正在制造的阶段，最后是一部成品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that carries raw material forward until it emerges as a finished box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把原料一路送到出口、变成成品箱的线。

branches.en: ACT AND SCALE: one factory's making and a whole economy's making are the same act at different sizes.
branches.cn: 动作与规模：一家工厂的制造与整个经济的制造，是同一动作的不同尺度。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND PHASE: the figure produced and the stage of being produced are two views of one process.
branches.cn: 数量与阶段：造出的数字与正在造的阶段，是同一过程的两种视角。

branches.en: STAGE: preparing a show and one finished staging are the process and its countable result.
branches.cn: 舞台：排演与一部成品，是过程与可数的结果。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: data and ideas are brought forth exactly as goods are.
branches.cn: 知识：数据和想法被带出来，与货物一样。

branches.en: BODY: a gland making a hormone is production with no factory at all.
branches.cn: 身体：腺体生成激素，是完全没有工厂的生产。

intro.en: Production is a Latin noun of leading forward, built from a prefix, a lead-root and an action ending.
intro.cn: production 是由「向前引出」构成的拉丁名词，包含前缀、引导词根与动作词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct, introduce, reduce and educate; pro- adds the forward direction that production keeps.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate；pro- 增添 production 保留的向前方向。

items.example: The prefix sends the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作送向外。

items.example: The root carries the pulling forward.
The verb produced the English produce.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出了英语的 produce。

items.example: The region produces most of the crop.
items.exampleCN: 该地区生产大部分这种作物。

items.example: The product sold out in a week.

items.exampleCN: 那是一个颇有成效的下午。

items.example: Productivity rose with the new tools.
items.exampleCN: 有了新工具，生产率提高了。
博物馆订了一件复制品。

definition_zh: 虚弱；弱点、缺陷；（对某事物的）偏爱、迷恋
definition_en: lack of strength, a fault in a person or thing, or a strong liking that is hard to resist
core_image: 一根细绳被拉得发紧，中间已经有了磨白的痕迹
scene: 老木桥的栏杆被人一靠就晃，木板缝里透出下面的河。 The weakness of the old bridge was obvious to anyone who looked closely.
sceneCN: 这里 weakness 是「弱点、缺陷」（第 2 个义项：人或事物不够牢固的地方）；句意为任何人只要看仔细些，都能发现这座老桥的弱点。磨白的绳痕，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：虚弱、无力；弱点、缺陷；偏爱

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根形容词，义为「虚弱的；薄弱的」
加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「削弱；变弱」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「虚弱地；无力地」
由 weak 加 -ing 构成，义为「体弱者」（口语罕用）

senses.title: Lack of physical strength
senses.definition: the state of lacking physical strength or energy
senses.definitionCN: 缺少体力或精力的状态
senses.example: After the fever, a deep weakness stayed in his legs for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后，他双腿的虚弱感持续了好几周。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns an adjective into a state; weakness is simply the state of being weak.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成状态；weakness 就是「弱」这一状态。

senses.title: A fault in a person
senses.definition: a fault or defect in someone's character, such as impatience or pride
senses.definitionCN: 某人性格中的欠缺，如急躁或自负
senses.example: His one real weakness is that he cannot say no to a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 他唯一真正的弱点是无法拒绝朋友的请求。
senses.why: The adjective weak names a lack of strength; -ness turns that lack into a countable fault, one particular place where the strength runs out.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 weak 表示力量不足；后缀 -ness 把这种不足变成可数的缺点，即力量耗尽的某一处。

senses.title: A weak point in a thing
senses.titleCN: 缺陷：事物中不牢固的地方
senses.definition: a part of a system, structure or argument that is not strong or convincing
senses.definitionCN: 系统、结构或论证中不够牢固、不够有说服力的部分
senses.example: Engineers found a weakness where the two beams meet.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师发现两根梁相接之处的薄弱点。
senses.why: The same noun moves from people to things: any structure is judged by its least strong part.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从人移到物：任何结构都以最不牢固的部分来评判。

senses.title: A strong liking
senses.definition: a strong liking for something that one finds hard to resist
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈而难以抗拒的喜爱
senses.example: She has a weakness for old watches.
senses.exampleCN: 她对旧手表有一种偏爱。
senses.why: Here the fault turns inward and pleasant: a liking you cannot resist is a weak spot in your self-control.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺陷转向内里且变得愉快：抵挡不住的喜爱，正是自制力上的薄弱处。

senses.title: Lack of force or authority
senses.titleCN: 软弱无力：力量或权威不足
senses.definition: lack of strength in a government, argument or action, so that it has little effect
senses.definitionCN: 政府、论证或行动缺乏力度，因而收效甚微
senses.example: The weakness of the new law was clear from the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 新法的软弱无力在头一个月就显露出来。
senses.why: Weakness of a law or a case means it cannot stand up to challenge, the same image of strength running out.
senses.whyCN: 法律或论证的软弱，指它经不起挑战，仍是力量耗尽的同一意象。

intro.en: Weakness is a native English compound of the old adjective weak and the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: weakness 是本族英语复合词，由古老形容词 weak 与名词后缀 -ness 组成。

items.en: The adjective veikr meant 'pliant, weak'; it entered English from Norse rather than from Old English.
items.cn: 形容词 veikr 意为「柔软的、弱的」，是从古诺尔斯语而非古英语进入英语的。

items.en: Old English had its own wac, meaning 'weak, pliant', related to the verb wican 'to give way'.
items.cn: 古英语自有 wac，意为「弱的、柔软的」，与动词 wican「退让」相关。

items.en: The two forms merged into the single adjective weik or weak in the north of England first.
items.cn: 两种形式合并为单一形容词，先在英格兰北部写成 weik 或 weak。

items.en: The suffix -nesse was fully productive, so weakness appeared as soon as the adjective was established.
items.cn: 后缀 -nesse 当时构词能力很强，形容词一成形，weakness 便随之出现。

items.en: The figurative senses, a fault and a fondness, are later extensions of the same state.
items.cn: 「缺陷」与「迷恋」两个比喻义，是同一种状态后来伸出的延伸。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the weak family; the near-meaning group gathers words for faults and for fondness.
note.cn: 形近组收 weak 一族词；近义组收表示缺陷与偏爱的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for lacking strength; the base of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚弱的」，是名词的词根。

entries.definition: To make or become weaker.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「削弱；变弱」。

entries.definition: In a weak way; also an old adjective meaning sickly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「虚弱地」；也曾是表示「病弱的」形容词。

entries.definition: Seven days; a homophone with no connection in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星期」，与本词同音，来源无关。

entries.definition: A small fault that spoils something; sharper and more specific.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瑕疵、缺陷」，更尖锐也更具体。

entries.definition: A mistake or a defect for which someone can be blamed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「过错、缺点」，含可归咎之意。

entries.definition: Weakness of body or character, especially in old age.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脆弱」，多指年老体弱或性格弱点。

entries.definition: A minor weakness in a person's character.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺点」，多指性格上的小毛病。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old Norse veikr and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古诺尔斯语 veikr，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: weak plus -ness: the suffix simply names the state, so weakness is the state of being weak.
normal.cn: weak 加 -ness：后缀只是给状态命名，weakness 就是「弱」的状态。

normal.en: Strengths and weaknesses always come in pairs: an honest list has both.
normal.cn: 长处与短处总是成对出现：诚实的清单上两样都有。

normal.en: A weakness for chocolate is not a defect but a fondness.
normal.cn: a weakness for chocolate 不是缺陷，而是一种偏爱。

normal.en: Weakness in an argument is a gap where evidence should be.
normal.cn: 论证中的 weakness 就是本该有证据的空缺。

normal.en: Week is a homophone and means seven days; weakness means no strength.
normal.cn: week 同音，指七天；weakness 指没有力气。

abstract.en: Picture a rope worn pale in the middle: the weak point is where the strain shows first.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子中间磨得发白：弱点就是拉力最先显形的地方。

abstract.en: The word works for bodies, buildings, arguments and hearts, because all can give way under pressure.
abstract.cn: 这个词适用于身体、建筑、论证和人心，因为它们在压力下都可能让步。

abstract.en: Finding a weakness is not an insult; it is where a repair or a defence belongs.
abstract.cn: 找到弱点并不是侮辱，那正是修补或防守该落脚的地方。

examples.en: Weakness in the knees made the climb dangerous.
examples.cn: 膝盖无力让这次攀登变得危险。

examples.en: Every plan has a weakness, and this one is the budget.
examples.cn: 每个计划都有薄弱处，这个计划的薄弱处就是预算。

examples.en: He has a weakness for cheap second-hand books.
examples.cn: 他对便宜的二手书有种偏爱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唯一（wei）克（k）尼斯（ness）」——唯一被克制的尼斯湖怪，因为太虚弱：虚弱

root: 由古诺尔斯语 veikr「柔软的、弱的」与古英语 wac 合流而成的 weak，加名词后缀 -ness 构成；同族词有 weaken、weakly、weakling。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weakness begin with the plain state of no strength, then name a fault in a person, a gap in a thing, a fondness, and a general lack of force.
sensesIntro.cn: weakness 的五个义项始于「没有力气」这一朴素状态，继而指人的缺点、事物的空隙、一种偏爱，以及普遍的力量不足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope worn pale in the middle where the strain shows first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根中间磨得发白的绳子，拉力最先在那里显形。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the muscles have no force left.
branches.cn: 身体线：肌肉再也使不出力。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: a person cannot resist a certain impulse.
branches.cn: 性格线：人抗拒不了某种冲动。

branches.en: STRUCTURE LINE: a beam, a law or an argument lacks force.
branches.cn: 结构线：梁、法条或论证缺乏力度。

branches.en: DESIRE LINE: the same word turns kind, naming a fondness.
branches.cn: 欲望线：同一个词转得温柔，指一种偏爱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: flaw is sharper, failing is gentler, weakness is the plainest.
branches.cn: 对照线：flaw 更尖锐，failing 更温和，weakness 最朴素。

intro.en: Weakness is a Germanic adjective plus the native -ness suffix; no Latin element is involved.
intro.cn: weakness 是日耳曼语形容词加本族的 -ness 后缀，不涉及拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.exampleCN: 它是 wac 背后的古老动词。

definition_zh: 建议；意见；暗示
definition_en: an idea offered to others, or a slight hint of something
core_image: 桌上一张便签，写着「要不要试试这样」
scene: 他的建议帮助我们解决了问题。 His suggestion helped us solve the problem.

senses.title: Idea offered
senses.definition: an idea or plan offered for others to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出供别人考虑的想法或计划
senses.example: His suggestion helped us solve the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他的建议帮助我们解决了问题。
senses.why: This is the main everyday sense.

senses.title: Hint
senses.definition: something that hints at an idea
senses.definitionCN: 暗示某种想法的事物
senses.example: There was a suggestion of anger in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音里有一丝怒气。
senses.why: Here the word points to an indirect sign.
senses.whyCN: 这里指间接的迹象。

senses.title: Faint trace
senses.definition: a very small amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物极少的量
senses.example: The sauce has a suggestion of garlic.
senses.exampleCN: 这酱汁里有一点点蒜味。
senses.why: Only a trace is present.
senses.whyCN: 这里只存在极少的痕迹。

definition_zh: 后者的；后半的；后期的
definition_en: referring to the second of two things already mentioned; belonging to the later part of a period; recent or modern in a formal phrase
core_image: 两张并排的卡片，手指落在右边那一张上
scene: 桌上摊着两份方案，他看了一会儿，把手指落在右边那份更薄的纸上。 Of the two plans, the latter seemed cheaper and far simpler.
sceneCN: 这里是「后者的」（第 1 个义项：两个事物中的第二个）；句意是两份方案里，后者看起来更便宜也简单得多。图中可辨识物件：两份方案、桌面、手指。

collocations.zh: 在晚年；在后来的岁月里

derivatives.zh: 由 latter 加 -ly 构成，义为「在后期；最近」
由 latter 与 day 复合而成，义为「晚期的；现代的」

senses.title: The second of two things mentioned
senses.definition: the second of two people or things just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 刚提到的两个人或事物中的第二个
senses.example: Of the two plans, the latter seemed cheaper and far simpler.
senses.exampleCN: 两份方案里，后者看起来更便宜也简单得多。
senses.why: The Old English comparative meant later, and when two things are listed in order the later one is the second, which is how the contrast with former arose.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的比较级意为「更晚的」，而两个事物按顺序列出时，较晚的那个就是第二个，与 former 的对举便由此形成。

senses.title: The later part of a period
senses.definition: belonging to the later part of a period or process
senses.definitionCN: 属于某段时期或过程的靠后部分
senses.example: The latter half of the book is far more exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书的后半部分要精彩得多。
senses.why: A period can be split into an earlier and a later part, so the old comparative of late naturally labels the second half.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间可以分成较早与较晚两部分，于是 late 的旧比较级自然被用来标记后半段。

senses.title: Recent or modern, in formal phrasing
senses.definition: recent or modern, especially in fixed phrases such as latter-day
senses.definitionCN: 近来的或现代的，尤见于 latter-day 这类固定说法
senses.example: He writes about latter-day heroes and their small daily battles.
senses.exampleCN: 他写的是现代英雄以及他们日常的小小战斗。
senses.why: What is later in time is also nearer to the present, so latter came to describe recent or modern things in formal usage.
senses.whyCN: 时间上更晚的也离现在更近，所以 latter 在正式用法里逐渐指近来或现代的事物。

intro.en: Latter is the old comparative of late, a Germanic word; English has kept it mainly for the second of two and for the later part of something.
intro.cn: latter 是 late 的旧比较级，而 late 是日耳曼语词；英语主要用它指两者中的后者和某事物的后半段。

items.en: Late goes back to a Germanic word for slow or sluggish, and its comparative had a form of its own.
items.cn: late 可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「慢、迟缓」的词，它的比较级另有形态。

items.en: Old English lætra was the comparative of læt and meant later or more slow.
items.cn: 古英语 lætra 是 læt 的比较级，意为更晚或更慢。

items.en: Middle English latter kept the comparative meaning and began to pair with former.
items.cn: 中古英语 latter 保留比较级含义，并开始与 former 对举。

items.en: Printing and formal prose fixed the pair the former and the latter for two things already named.
items.cn: 印刷术与正式散文把 the former 与 the latter 固定为指两个已提及事物的配对。

items.en: Modern English also uses latter for the later part of a period and for latter-day ideas.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 latter 指时期的后半段，以及 latter-day 这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms of late and compounds of latter; the near-meaning group collects words that order or oppose two things.
note.cn: 形近组收 late 的各种形式与 latter 的复合词；近义组收给两者排序或作对照的词。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or after something else; the ordinary comparative of late.
entries.definitionCN: 在现在或某事之后的某个时间；late 的普通比较级。

entries.definition: Most recent in time; the superlative of late.
entries.definitionCN: 时间上最近的；late 的最高级。

entries.definition: Recently, or in the later part of a period.
entries.definitionCN: 最近，或在某段时期的后期。

entries.definition: Modern or recent, often used of a new version of an old type.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的或近来的，常指旧类型的新版本。

entries.definition: The first of two things mentioned; the direct partner of latter.
entries.definitionCN: 两个被提到的事物中的第一个；与 latter 直接配对。

entries.definition: Coming before the one now mentioned or current.
entries.definitionCN: 在现在提到或当前这个之前的。

entries.definition: Final in order, or most recent before the present.
entries.definitionCN: 顺序上的最后一个，或现在之前最近的。

entries.definition: Coming at the end of a series or process.
entries.definitionCN: 处在一串事物或过程末尾的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a frozen comparative, so its memory hooks are the pairing with former and the family of late forms around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个凝固的比较级，所以记忆抓手是与 former 的配对，以及周围 late 的各种形式。

normal.en: Latter and former are a fixed pair: former names the first of two, latter names the second.
normal.cn: latter 与 former 是固定配对：former 指两个中的第一个，latter 指第二个。

normal.en: Latter is not the same as later: later is about time, while latter is about position in a list of two.
normal.cn: latter 与 later 不同：later 谈时间，latter 谈两项列表中的位置。

normal.en: Latterly adds -ly to latter and means recently or in the later part of a period.
normal.cn: latterly 在 latter 后加 -ly，意为最近或某段时期的后期。

normal.en: Latter-day is a compound meaning modern, often suggesting a new version of something old.
normal.cn: latter-day 是表示「现代的」的复合词，常暗示旧事物的新版本。

normal.en: The word keeps an old comparative shape, which is why it has no comparative or superlative of its own.
normal.cn: 这个词保留了古老的比较级形态，所以它本身没有比较级或最高级。

abstract.en: Two things side by side create an order, and a language needs a short word for the second one.
abstract.cn: 两个事物并排就产生了顺序，而语言需要一个短词来指第二个。

abstract.en: Latter turns position into time: the second in a list is also the one that comes later.
abstract.cn: latter 把位置变成时间：列表中的第二个也是来得较晚的那一个。

abstract.en: A word that refuses to be compared reminds us that some grammatical forms are fossils of older stages.
abstract.cn: 一个拒绝再被比较的词提醒人：有些语法形式是更早阶段的化石。

examples.cn: 这本书的后半部分要精彩得多。

examples.en: She chose the latter option without a moment's doubt.
examples.cn: 她毫不犹豫地选了后一个选项。

sensesIntro.en: The core is second position in a pair; it extends to the later half of a period and to recent or modern things.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是成对事物中的第二位；由此延伸到一段时期的后半段，以及近来或现代的事物。

definition_zh: 完全地；彻底地；整个地
definition_en: completely and in every way; absolutely

scene: 看到考试成绩，她惊讶地喊道： I totally forgot we had a test today!

senses.title: Completely; in every way

senses.title: Absolutely in speech

senses.example: Totally! That's exactly what I was thinking.

senses.why: Daily speech borrows the extreme degree as an exclamation of full agreement.

definition_zh: 领导；领导能力；领导层；领导地位
definition_en: the ability or activity of guiding a group, or the people who hold that role
core_image: 队伍最前面的人举着火把，后面的人跟着那点光走，暗处的路看不清
scene: 夜路上，走在最前面的人举着火把，后面的人跟着那点光前进。 Her leadership turned a divided committee into a working team.
sceneCN: 这里指「带领群体行动的领导能力」（第 1 个义项：引导群体的能力）；句意为她的领导力把一个分裂的委员会变成了能运转的团队。可辨识物件：火把、夜路、队伍、前方拐角、脚印。

pos.zh: 领导；领导能力（常作不可数）
领导层；领导班子（集合名词）

collocations.zh: 思想领导力；行业思想权威

forms.label: 可数用法（领导层，少见复数）

derivatives.zh: 带领（过去式与过去分词）

senses.title: The ability to guide a group
senses.definition: the capacity to set a direction and keep a group working toward it
senses.definitionCN: 确定方向并使一个群体朝该方向持续行动的能力
senses.example: Her leadership turned a divided committee into a working team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的领导力把一个分裂的委员会变成了能运转的团队。
senses.why: The verb behind the word means 'to cause to go'; leadership is the ability to make a group go in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的动词意为「使行走」；领导力就是使一个群体朝同一方向前进的能力。

senses.title: The position of leader
senses.definition: the office or role of being the person who directs a group
senses.definitionCN: 指导一个群体的那个人所占据的职位或角色
senses.example: He assumed leadership of the party after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，他接任了该党的领导职务。
senses.why: The suffix turns a person into a state: being a leader is a role that can be entered and left.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把人变成一种状态：做领导者是一个可以进入也可以离开的角色。

senses.title: The group at the top
senses.definition: the collective body of people who hold the highest directing roles in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织中占据最高指导职位的集体
senses.example: The leadership met behind closed doors before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之前，领导层闭门开会。
senses.why: English often treats a set of office-holders as one collective noun, so the role becomes a body.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一群任职者当作一个集合名词，于是职位变成了一个机构。

senses.title: A way of leading
senses.definition: a characteristic manner of directing others, such as coaching, directing or delegating
senses.definitionCN: 指导他人的典型方式，如教练式、指挥式或授权式
senses.example: A coaching style of leadership improved staff retention.
senses.exampleCN: 教练式的领导风格提高了员工留任率。
senses.why: Once leadership is studied, its manners are classified, and each one becomes a named style.
senses.whyCN: 一旦领导被研究，它的做法就会被分类，每一种做法都成为一个有名称的风格。

senses.title: Direction at the level of government
senses.definition: the activity of setting public direction and taking responsibility for national or local decisions
senses.definitionCN: 确定公共方向并为国家或地方决策承担责任的活动
senses.example: Political leadership was slow to recognize the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 政治领导层迟迟没有认识到旱情的严重。
senses.why: The word moves easily from a team to a state, because both need someone to set a course.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很容易从团队移到国家，因为两者都需要有人确定航向。

senses.title: Authority of ideas in an industry
senses.definition: the reputation of shaping how an industry thinks, often built through research and public comment
senses.definitionCN: 塑造一个行业思考方式的声誉，常通过研究与公开发言建立
senses.example: The firm publishes reports to establish thought leadership in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司发布报告，以在该领域建立思想领导力。
senses.why: Leading need not mean commanding; whoever defines the questions can lead an industry's attention.
senses.whyCN: 领导不必意味着命令；能界定问题的人就能引导一个行业的注意力。

senses.title: First place in a market
senses.definition: the position of having the largest share or the strongest reputation in a market
senses.definitionCN: 在市场中获得最大份额或最强声誉的位置
senses.example: The brand lost market leadership after the recall.
senses.exampleCN: 召回事件之后，这个品牌失去了市场领先地位。
senses.why: Competition borrows the image of a race: the leader is simply the one furthest ahead.
senses.whyCN: 竞争借用了赛跑的意象：领先者就是跑在最前面的那一个。

senses.title: Keeping a group together in difficulty
senses.titleCN: 困境中维持群体的凝聚
senses.definition: the work of holding a group together and making it continue when conditions are hard
senses.definitionCN: 在艰难条件下维持群体并使其继续前进的工作
senses.example: Leadership in a storm means keeping the group together, not walking fastest.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴中的领导意味着让队伍保持在一起，而不是自己走得最快。
senses.why: The oldest image is a person walking ahead with a light; the point is not speed but that others can still follow.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是一个人举着光走在前面；重点不是速度，而是后来的人仍能跟上。

intro.en: Leadership joins leader with the noun suffix -ship. Leader comes from the verb lead, from Old English lǣdan 'to lead, guide', a causative form related to līþan 'to go, travel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: leadership 由 leader 加名词后缀构成。leader 来自动词 lead，后者出自古英语 lǣdan「带领、引导」，是与 līþan「行走、旅行」相关的使役形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Līþan meant 'to go, travel'. Its earlier Germanic source is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: līþan 意为「行走、旅行」。它在日耳曼语中更早的来源属于重构，而非直接有据。

items.en: Lǣdan was the causative partner of līþan, meaning 'to make go, conduct, guide'.
items.cn: lǣdan 是 līþan 的使役对应词，意为「使行走、引导、带领」。

items.en: The verb lead survived into Middle English and extended from guiding people to being first in a race or market.
items.cn: 动词 lead 进入中古英语，并从引导人扩展到在竞赛或市场中领先。

items.en: Leader named the person who conducts others, formed from the verb with an agent ending.
items.cn: leader 指带领他人的人，由动词加施事后缀构成。

items.en: The ending -ship comes from Old English -scipe, meaning 'state or condition', so leadership is the state of being a leader.
items.cn: 这个名词后缀来自古英语中表示「状态或境况」的相应后缀，因此 leadership 就是身为领导者的状态。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Germanic source of līþan is a reconstruction, and no exact first citation is fixed for the modern managerial sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：līþan 在日耳曼语之前的来源属于重构形式；现代管理义也没有确切的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same guiding family in other grammatical roles; group two holds nouns for directing people and work.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「引导」词族、语法角色不同的词；第二组是指挥人与工作的名词。

entries.definition: The person who guides a group; leadership is the role, ability or body that surrounds that person.
entries.definitionCN: 引导群体的人；leadership 是围绕这个人的角色、能力或集体。

entries.definition: To guide or be first; it names the action from which the noun is built.
entries.definitionCN: 引导或处于首位；它指构成这个名词的动作。

entries.definition: Means guiding or being ahead; as an adjective it describes the front position.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「引导的」或「领先的」；作形容词时描述最前的位置。

entries.definition: To guide someone in the wrong direction; it shares the same walking root but adds a prefix of error.
entries.definitionCN: 把人引向错误方向；共享同一个「行走」词根，只是加上表示错误的前缀。

entries.definition: The activity of planning and controlling resources; leadership sets direction, management maintains the system.
entries.definitionCN: 计划与控制资源的活动；领导确定方向，管理维持系统。

entries.definition: Advice or direction given to someone who needs to find a path; it is usually less formal than leadership.
entries.definitionCN: 给需要找路的人以建议或方向；通常比 leadership 更不正式。

entries.definition: The course or line along which something moves; leadership is the act of setting that course.
entries.definitionCN: 某物前进的路线或方向；leadership 是设定这条路线的行为。

entries.definition: Recognized power to command; a leader may have authority, but leadership can exist without it.
entries.definitionCN: 被承认的命令权；领导者可以拥有权威，但领导力也能在没有权威时存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real walking root, the real suffix and the real organizational phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「行走」词根、真实的后缀与真实的组织搭配。

normal.en: The verb means 'to cause to go', so leadership is the ability to make a group go forward together.
normal.cn: 动词意为「使行走」，因此领导力就是使一个群体共同前进的能力。

normal.en: The suffix means 'state or condition', so leadership is literally the state of being a leader.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「状态或境况」，因此 leadership 字面上就是身为领导者的状态。

normal.en: The family runs lead, leader, leading, led, leadership and mislead.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lead、leader、leading、led、leadership 与 mislead。

normal.en: The organizational phrases are under the leadership of, strong leadership and leadership style.
normal.cn: 组织搭配有在……的领导下、强有力的领导与领导风格。

normal.en: The political and business phrases are party leadership, market leadership and thought leadership.
normal.cn: 政治与商业搭配有党的领导层、市场领先地位与思想领导力。

abstract.en: Picture a torch at the front of a night column, visible just far enough to follow.
abstract.cn: 想象夜行队伍最前面的一支火把，光刚好够后面的人跟着走。

abstract.en: Picture a committee split into two rooms until one person brings both back to the same table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会分裂在两个房间，直到有人把双方带回同一张桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a storm where the slowest walker sets the pace and no one is left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一场风暴，最慢的人决定速度，没有人被落下。

examples.en: The school needs stable leadership before it can change the curriculum.
examples.cn: 学校需要稳定的领导层，才能改变课程。

examples.en: She studied leadership in small teams rather than in large corporations.
examples.cn: 她研究的是小团队中的领导，而非大公司中的领导。

examples.en: Under his leadership, the clinic doubled the number of patients it could see.
examples.cn: 在他的领导下，诊所能够接诊的病人数量翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「带领」加「身份状态」——走在最前面并让后面的人跟上来 → 领导、领导力

root: leadership 由 leader 加名词后缀构成。leader 来自动词 lead，出自古英语 lǣdan「带领」，与 līþan「行走」相关的使役形式；这个名词后缀来自古英语中表示「状态」的相应后缀。更早的日耳曼来源属于重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: someone walks in front with a light. The image becomes an ability, a position, a body of leaders, a manner, a government's direction, an industry's authority, a market's first place and finally the work of keeping a group together in a storm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：有人举着光走在前面。这个意象依次变成能力、职位、领导班子、方式、政府的方向、行业的思想权威、市场的首位，最后是在风暴中维持群体不散的工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a torch carried at the head of a night column.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜行队伍最前面的一支火把。

branches.en: THE ABILITY: the first sense is the capacity to set a direction and keep others moving.
branches.cn: 能力：第一个义项是确定方向并使他人持续前进的能力。

branches.en: THE ROLE AND THE STORM: holding the office and holding the group together are two sides of the same walk.
branches.cn: 职位与风暴：占据职位与维持群体不散，是同一次行走的两面。

branches.en: THE BODY: a set of office-holders becomes a collective noun with its own meetings.
branches.cn: 集体：一群任职者变成一个拥有自己会议的集合名词。

branches.en: THE MANNER AND THE MIND: coaching a team and shaping an industry's questions are both ways of leading.
branches.cn: 方式与思想：教练一个团队与塑造一个行业的问题，都是领导的方式。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC RACE: a government sets a national course, and a brand runs first in its market.
branches.cn: 公共赛跑：政府确定国家航向，品牌在其市场中跑在最前。

intro.en: The noun can be read from an Old English verb of going, its causative partner, an agent noun and the suffix of state.
intro.cn: 这个名词可以按表示行走的古英语动词、它的使役对应词、施事名词以及表示状态的后缀逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: This word is native English rather than Latin: the Germanic walking root supplies lead, leader and leadership, and the state suffix comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词而非拉丁借词：日耳曼语中表示行走的词根衍生 lead、leader 与 leadership，表示状态的后缀来自古英语。

items.example: The old verb named ordinary movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词指普通的移动。

items.example: The causative verb added the idea of causing others to move.
items.exampleCN: 这个使役动词增添了使他人移动的意思。

items.example: She led the group through the pass.
The leader set the pace for the climb.
The leading runner never looked back.
items.exampleCN: 跑在最前面的选手从未回头。

items.example: The guide led us to the ridge.

items.meaning: the state or activity of leading
items.example: The team needed leadership after the loss.
items.exampleCN: 失利之后，这个团队需要领导。

items.example: The suffix turns a person into a role.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一个人变成一种角色。

items.meaning: to guide in the wrong direction
items.example: The sign misled drivers into the closed road.
items.exampleCN: 那块牌子把司机引进了封闭的道路。

definition_zh: 部；内阁部门；内阁；执政期；牧师职务；神职
definition_en: a government department headed by a minister, the government as a whole, or the office and work of a religious minister
core_image: 一栋办公楼的门旁挂着铜牌，牌上只刻一个部门的名字
scene: 教堂旁边的办公楼里，工作人员把一份新规定贴上公告栏，纸角压着一个部门印章。 The ministry published the new rules on its website.
sceneCN: 这里 ministry 是「政府部门、部」（第 1 个义项：由部长主管的政府机关）；句意为该部门在网站上公布了新规定。画面里可抓住的物件：公告栏、部门印章、办公楼铜牌。

pos.zh: 部；内阁部门；内阁；执政期；牧师职务；神职

derivatives.zh: 与 ministry 同一词干，指担任职务的人，义为「部长；大臣；牧师」
由 minister 加 -ial 构成，义为「部长的；内阁的；牧师的」
由拉丁 ministrare 加 -ant 构成，指「服侍者；主持仪式的」
由拉丁 administrare 加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政」

senses.title: A government department
senses.definition: a department of government led by a minister and responsible for one area of public life
senses.definitionCN: 由部长领导、负责某一方面公共事务的政府部门
senses.example: The Ministry of Health issued new guidance on masks.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生部发布了关于口罩的新指引。
senses.why: Latin ministerium meant service or office; when a minister took charge of an area of public service, the office itself came to be called a ministry.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ministerium 意为「服务、职务」；当部长主管某一方面的公共事务时，那个职务机构本身就被称为 ministry。

senses.title: The government or its term in office
senses.definition: a government led by a prime minister, or the period during which it holds power
senses.definitionCN: 由总理或首相领导的一届政府，或它掌权的时期
senses.example: The ministry fell after losing a vote of confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁在失去信任投票后倒台。
senses.why: Because a ministry is the whole set of ministers serving together, the word shifted from one department to the cabinet and to the time it stays in power.
senses.whyCN: 因为 ministry 也指共同任职的一整批部长，词义便从一个部门转到整个内阁，再转到它掌权的时期。

senses.title: The office of a religious minister
senses.definition: the profession or work of an ordained religious minister, or the clergy as a body
senses.definitionCN: 受按立牧师的职业与工作，或作为整体的神职人员
senses.example: She left teaching to enter the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开教职，进入神职。
senses.why: The same Latin word for service was applied to the church, where ministry names the work of serving a congregation rather than a government office.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「服务」的拉丁词也被用到教会，这里的 ministry 指服侍会众的工作，而不是政府机关。

intro.en: Ministry is the office built on the Latin noun for service, and English uses it for both a government department and the work of the church.
intro.cn: ministry 是建立在拉丁语「服务」名词之上的职务，英语用它兼指政府部门与教会工作。

items.en: Minister meant a servant or attendant, and everything built on it keeps the idea of service.
items.cn: minister 指仆人或随从，凡由它构成的词都保留了「服务」的观念。

items.en: Ministerium named service, office or function, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: ministerium 指服务、职务或职能，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the word as menistere, meaning office or service, before it passed into English.
items.cn: 古法语把它写作 menistere，意为职务或服务，随后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English ministry covered service and the work of the clergy, and the political sense joined it later.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ministry 覆盖服务与神职工作，政治义后来才加入。

items.en: Modern English uses ministry for a department of state, for a whole government, and for the religious vocation.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ministry 指国家部门、整个内阁，以及宗教使命。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of service and management; the near-meaning group collects names for departments, cabinets and clergy.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「服务、管理」词干上的词；近义组收部门、内阁与神职人员的名称。

entries.definition: The person who heads a department or leads a congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 主管一个部门或带领会众的人。

entries.definition: Relating to a minister or to a government department.
entries.definitionCN: 与部长或政府部门有关的。

entries.definition: To manage affairs or to put a rule or treatment into effect.
entries.definitionCN: 管理事务，或施行某项规则、治疗。

entries.definition: The act of serving or assisting, especially in worship.
entries.definitionCN: 服侍或协助的行为，尤指在礼拜中。

entries.definition: A division of a government or a large organization.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或大型机构中的一个部门。

entries.definition: The group of senior ministers who advise a prime minister or president.
entries.definitionCN: 为首相或总统提供建议的一批高级部长。

entries.definition: The body of ordained religious leaders.
entries.definitionCN: 受按立的宗教领袖全体。

entries.definition: A government office or a division of one.
entries.definitionCN: 政府机关或其中的一个部门。

normalIntro.en: Ministry is the office that grows out of a minister's service, and the family keeps the same Latin stem in view.
normalIntro.cn: ministry 是从 minister 的服务中长出来的职务机构，整族词都共用同一个拉丁词干。

normal.en: Ministry is built on minister, the person; the -y ending turns the servant into the office he or she holds.
normal.cn: ministry 建立在 minister 这个「人」之上；-y 词尾把仆人变成他所担任的职务。

normal.en: Latin ministerium meant service or function, so ministry is literally the job rather than the building.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ministerium 意为服务或职能，所以 ministry 字面上是那份工作，而不是那栋楼。

normal.en: Ministry of Education, foreign ministry and ministry of defence all show the word naming a branch of government.
normal.cn: Ministry of Education、foreign ministry 与 ministry of defence 都展示了这个词如何命名政府的一个分支。

normal.en: Enter the ministry is a fixed phrase for becoming an ordained minister, where the word means vocation rather than department.
normal.cn: enter the ministry 是成为按立牧师的固定说法，这里的词义是使命而非部门。

normal.en: Administration and administer share the same ministrare root, so the whole family is about handling affairs for someone else.
normal.cn: administration 与 administer 共用 ministrare 这个词根，所以整族词都与替别人经办事务有关。

abstract.en: Picture a brass plate on a door: one word names the people inside, the work they do and the time they hold office.
abstract.cn: 想象门上一块铜牌：一个词同时说出里面的人、他们做的事，以及他们任职的时间。

abstract.en: A ministry is a service organized into an office, whether the service is to the state or to a congregation.
abstract.cn: ministry 是被组织成机构的服务，无论对象是国家还是会众。

abstract.en: One Latin noun for service grows into a department, a cabinet and a calling without changing its stem.
abstract.cn: 一个表示服务的拉丁名词长成部门、内阁与使命，词干始终没变。

examples.en: The Ministry of Health issued new guidance on masks.
examples.cn: 卫生部发布了关于口罩的新指引。

examples.en: The ministry fell after losing a vote of confidence.
examples.cn: 内阁在失去信任投票后倒台。

examples.en: She left teaching to enter the ministry.
examples.cn: 她离开教职，进入神职。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你斯特里」——再迷你的部门也要办正事，一栋楼、一群人、一个部长；ministry 是部、内阁部门。

root: 拉丁语 ministerium（服务、职务）源自 minister（仆人、随从）；经古法语进入英语，先指服侍与神职，后指政府部门与内阁。

sensesIntro.en: The core is service organized as an office; the senses run from a single department to the whole cabinet and to the religious vocation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被组织成机构的服务；各义项从单个部门走到整个内阁，再到宗教使命。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass nameplate on a government building, with one department's name and a seal beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：政府大楼门旁的铜牌，刻着一个部门的名字，下面压着印章。

branches.en: a nameplate for one department on a ministry door
branches.cn: 部门门口只刻一个部门名的铜牌

branches.en: ministers seated around a cabinet table
branches.cn: 围坐内阁桌旁的一排部长

branches.en: a young pastor being ordained before a congregation
branches.cn: 在会众面前受按立的年轻牧师

branches.en: a department that speaks for the whole government
branches.cn: 代表整个政府发声的部门

branches.en: one word holding both a political term and a calling
branches.cn: 一个词同时装下政治任期与宗教使命

intro.en: Ministry is the office formed from the Latin noun for service, and its items trace how a job becomes an institution.
intro.cn: ministry 是由拉丁语「服务」名词形成的职务机构，各构词条目串起「工作变成制度」的过程。

latinIntro.en: Ministry comes from the Latin noun for service and office, and the same stem is behind minister and administer.
latinIntro.cn: ministry 来自表示「服务、职务」的拉丁名词，同一词干也支撑着 minister 与 administer。

definition_zh: 耐心；耐性；毅力；单人纸牌游戏
definition_en: the ability to accept delay or trouble without becoming angry, the steady persistence needed for a long task, or a card game played by one person
core_image: 孩子弯着腰，一遍遍重系那根鞋带
scene: 孩子坐在门槛上，一遍遍把散开的鞋带重新系好，母亲在门口看着。 Learning to tie a knot takes patience.
sceneCN: 这里的 patience 是「耐心、耐性」（第 1 个义项：能平静地等待与重复）；句意是学会系结需要耐心。图中可辨识物件：门槛、散开的鞋带、孩子的双手。

pos.zh: 耐心；耐性；毅力；单人纸牌游戏

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 patiens 经古法语进入英语，义为「有耐心的」；与 patience 同源
由 patient 加 -ly 构成，义为「耐心地」
由否定前缀 im- 加 patient 构成，义为「不耐烦的」

senses.title: The ability to wait calmly
senses.definition: the ability to accept delay, trouble or suffering without becoming angry or upset
senses.definitionCN: 能够接受延误、麻烦或痛苦而不发怒、不烦躁的能力
senses.example: Learning to tie a knot takes patience.
senses.exampleCN: 学会系结需要耐心。
senses.why: Patience comes from Latin pati, to suffer, so waiting well is a mild form of bearing something unpleasant rather than a blank absence of feeling.
senses.whyCN: patience 出自拉丁语 pati（忍受），所以好好等待是一种轻微地承受不快，而不是没有感觉的空白。

senses.title: Steady persistence in a long task
senses.definition: the quality of continuing with something difficult for a long time without losing interest
senses.definitionCN: 长时间坚持做困难的事而不失去兴趣的品质
senses.example: Her patience with the experiment finally paid off.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这项实验的坚持终于有了回报。
senses.why: Endurance is not only waiting but continuing, and the same Latin root covers both because each one keeps bearing a cost as time passes.
senses.whyCN: 忍耐不只是等，还包括继续做下去；同一个拉丁词根同时覆盖两者，因为二者都在时间里持续承担代价。

senses.title: A card game for one player
senses.definition: a card game played by one person, known in American English as solitaire
senses.definitionCN: 一个人玩的纸牌游戏，美式英语中称为 solitaire
senses.example: He laid out a game of patience on the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房桌上摆开了一局单人纸牌。
senses.why: The game is named for the patience it demands: the player sits alone and waits for the right card to turn up.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏得名于它对耐心的要求：玩的人独自坐着，等待合适的那张牌翻出来。

intro.en: Patience comes from Latin patientia, the noun of enduring built on pati, to suffer; Old French passed it to English as pacience, where it named both calm endurance and, later, a solitary card game.
intro.cn: patience 来自拉丁语 patientia，这是由 pati（忍受）构成的表「忍耐」的名词；古法语把它写作 pacience 传入英语，先指平静的忍耐，后来也指一种单人纸牌游戏。

items.en: Pati was the verb for suffering, undergoing or putting up with something, and it is the root shared by patient and patience.
items.cn: pati 是表示受苦、经历、忍受的动词，是 patient 与 patience 共有的词根。

items.en: Patientia was the noun for endurance and forbearance, formed from the participle patiens plus the noun ending -entia.
items.cn: patientia 是表示忍耐与宽容的名词，由分词 patiens 加名词词尾 -entia 构成。

items.en: Old French kept the word as pacience, with the meaning of calm endurance under delay or pain.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 pacience，意为在延误或痛苦之下平静地忍耐。

items.en: Middle English patience covered calm waiting and the bearing of hardship; the card game was added to the word in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语的 patience 兼指平静的等待与对苦难的承受；单人纸牌这一义项在十八世纪才加上去。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun patience for the quality, while patient serves as the matching adjective and as a noun for a sick person.
items.cn: 现代英语用名词 patience 表示这种品质，而 patient 则作对应的形容词，也作名词指病人。

note.en: The look-alike group lays out the words built on the same Latin participle so the noun and the adjective are not confused; the near-meaning group gathers other names for endurance and calm.
note.cn: 形近组把建立在同一拉丁分词上的词并排摆开，免得把名词与形容词弄混；近义组收表示忍耐与平静的其他说法。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning able to wait calmly, and the noun for a sick person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词意为「有耐心的」，名词则指病人。

entries.definition: In a way that shows calm endurance of delay.
entries.definitionCN: 以平静忍耐延误的方式。

entries.definition: Unable to wait calmly, or eager for something to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 无法平静等待的，或急切盼望的。

entries.definition: The power to keep going through pain or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 在痛苦或艰难中坚持下去的力量。

entries.definition: The willingness to accept things one dislikes or disagrees with.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受自己不喜欢或不赞同之事的度量。

entries.definition: The act of continuing firmly despite difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 遇到困难仍坚定继续的行为。

entries.definition: A state of quietness in which anger and worry are absent.
entries.definitionCN: 没有怒气与焦虑的平静状态。

normalIntro.en: Patience is the noun of endurance built on the Latin verb to suffer, and its hooks show how bearing pain becomes calm waiting, long persistence and even a game played alone.
normalIntro.cn: patience 是建立在拉丁语「忍受」动词之上的表忍耐的名词，记忆钩子展示「承受痛苦」如何变成平静等待、长久坚持，乃至一个人的纸牌游戏。

normal.en: Pati is the Latin verb to suffer, so patience names the state of someone who bears something rather than someone who feels nothing.
normal.cn: pati 是拉丁语中「忍受」的动词，所以 patience 指承受着某物之人的状态，而不是毫无感觉。

normal.en: Patient is the adjective built on the participle patiens, while patience is the noun built on patientia; the pair differs in part of speech, not in root.
normal.cn: patient 是由分词 patiens 来的形容词，patience 是由 patientia 来的名词；这一对词性不同，词根相同。

normal.en: Impatient adds im-, meaning not, so an impatient person refuses to keep bearing the wait.
normal.cn: impatient 加上表示「不」的 im-，所以不耐烦的人是不肯继续承受等待的人。

normal.en: Patiently is patient plus -ly, and it describes the manner in which a delay is borne.
normal.cn: patiently 是 patient 加 -ly，描述的是承受延误的方式。

normal.en: The card game patience is named for the waiting it asks of a lone player, not for any rule of the game.
normal.cn: 纸牌游戏 patience 得名于它要求独自等待，而不是因为某条游戏规则。

abstract.en: Patience treats time as something that can be borne rather than spent, which is why the same word can mean waiting and persistence.
abstract.cn: patience 把时间看成可以承受的东西，而不是被花掉的东西，所以同一个词既能指等待，也能指坚持。

abstract.en: Because patience is a capacity, it can be kept, lost or worn thin, as if it were a material with a limited thickness.
abstract.cn: 因为 patience 是一种容量，它可以被保持、失去或磨薄，仿佛是一种厚度有限的材料。

abstract.en: The Latin root means to suffer, so patience is not indifference: it is endurance with the feeling left intact.
abstract.cn: 拉丁词根意为忍受，所以 patience 不是漠不关心：它是感觉仍然完好的忍耐。

examples.en: Learning to tie a knot takes patience.
examples.cn: 学会系结需要耐心。

examples.en: Her patience with the experiment finally paid off.
examples.cn: 她对这项实验的坚持终于有了回报。

examples.en: He laid out a game of patience on the kitchen table.
examples.cn: 他在厨房桌上摆开了一局单人纸牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪婶」——陪婶婶在车站等车，等再久也不催；记住 patience 是耐心。

core_image: 一只手在背后轻轻推着人往前

senses.title: To press someone to act
senses.definition: to try hard to make someone do something
senses.definitionCN: 努力使某人去做某事
senses.example: She urged him to see a doctor at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她力劝他立刻去看医生。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind it means to press or push, and pressing a person towards an act is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: 其拉丁动词意为「压、推」，把一个人朝某个行动推过去，就是它的第一层意思。

senses.title: To argue strongly for something
senses.definition: to recommend something forcefully in public or in writing
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合或文章里有力地主张某事
senses.example: The report urges stronger controls on waste.
senses.exampleCN: 报告竭力主张加强废物管控。
senses.why: A push made in words is still a push, and print carries it to many at once.
senses.whyCN: 用言语做出的推仍然是推，而文字能一次推给许多人。

senses.title: A strong wish to act
senses.definition: a strong feeling that one wants to do something
senses.definitionCN: 想做某事的强烈感受
senses.example: He felt a sudden urge to leave the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他突然想离开这个房间。
senses.why: The inner push that makes the urging possible is named by the same word, now as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 促成这种催促的内在推力，用同一个词作名词来表示。

senses.title: A physical need of the body
senses.definition: a need of the body that presses to be satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 身体上必须满足的需求
senses.example: The long ride gave the child an urgent urge to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 长途车让这孩子急着要停车。
senses.why: A body need presses harder than any advice, and the same word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 身体的某种需要比什么劝告都更急着逼人，这个词同样可以指它。

senses.title: Encouragement rather than order
senses.definition: used of support that moves a process on
senses.definitionCN: 形容推动某个进程前行的支持
senses.example: The teacher urged the class towards a harder question.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把全班往更难的问题上领。
senses.why: Pushing need not be harsh; a hand at the back also supports, and the word keeps that softer use.
senses.whyCN: 推并不一定是逼迫，背后那只手也在扶着，这个词保留了这层柔和用法。

senses.title: An impulse one must resist
senses.definition: used of a wish one struggles to control
senses.definitionCN: 形容努力想克制的念头
senses.example: She fought the urge to correct him in public.
senses.exampleCN: 她克制住了当场纠正他的念头。
senses.why: When the push comes from inside and no one asked for it, the impulse is something to be resisted.
senses.whyCN: 当推力来自内部、并非别人要求时，这股冲动就成了需要忍住的东西。

definition_zh: 追求；追捕；从事；继续进行；起诉；追随；探究；（对某人）热烈追求
definition_en: to follow someone or something closely, whether to catch it, to continue it, or to win it
core_image: 一个人紧贴着目标的后背跑，目标不停，他也不停——追捕、追梦、追案，都是同一条跑道
scene: 侦探望着巷子尽头，决定一直查到线索断掉为止。 We will pursue this case until the last lead runs out.
sceneCN: 这里 pursue 是「继续办理、坚持追查」（第 4 个义项：把事情一路跟到底）；句意：我们会一直追查这个案子，直到最后一条线索用完。画面里有雨巷、手电和翻开的卷宗；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 追求；追捕；从事；继续；起诉；追随

senses.title: To go after a goal: keep running toward it
senses.titleCN: 追求目标：一直朝着它跑
senses.definition: to try to achieve something over time, especially a goal, dream, or interest
senses.definitionCN: 长期努力实现某事，尤指目标、梦想或兴趣
senses.example: She moved to Berlin to pursue a career in music.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬到柏林去追求音乐事业。
senses.why: The 'seek, seek to obtain' sense is recorded in English in the late 14c. and was already present in Latin prosequi. A goal is treated as something ahead of you that you follow until you reach it, which is why the verb suits ambitions rather than wishes.
senses.whyCN: 「寻求、力求获得」这一义项在 14 世纪后期见于英语，拉丁语 prosequi 已有此义。目标被当成前方一个可以一路跟随、直到抵达的东西，所以这个词适合形容抱负，而不只是愿望。

senses.title: To chase down: follow with hostile intent
senses.titleCN: 追捕：带着敌意紧跟不放
senses.definition: to follow someone in order to catch or attack them
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟某人以抓住或攻击他
senses.example: Police pursued the stolen van through the narrow streets.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在窄巷里追捕那辆被盗的面包车。
senses.why: This is the word's first English sense (late 13c.): 'follow with hostile intent, follow with a view of overtaking'. The Latin ancestor prosequi meant 'follow after, escort', and hostile pursuit is that following turned aggressive.
senses.whyCN: 这是 pursue 最早的英语义项（13 世纪后期）：「带敌意跟随，意在赶上」。拉丁语祖先 prosequi 意为「跟随、护送」，敌意一起，跟随就变成了追捕。

senses.title: To practise: follow a trade or a subject
senses.titleCN: 从事：把一门职业或学问一路做下去
senses.definition: to engage in an activity, profession, or course of study over a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内从事某种活动、职业或学业
senses.example: He pursued medicine for twelve years before changing fields.
senses.exampleCN: 他从医十二年，之后才转行。
senses.why: A career or a subject is something you follow along a track rather than seize once. From 'seek to obtain' the verb widened to 'carry on with', and English says pursue medicine the way it says follow a path.
senses.whyCN: 职业或学问是沿着一条轨道跟随的东西，而不是一下子抓住的东西。动词从「力求获得」扩展到「持续进行」，所以英语说 pursue medicine，就像说 follow a path。

senses.title: To carry on: keep a course of action alive
senses.titleCN: 继续：把一件正在做的事做到底
senses.definition: to continue with an activity, plan, or course of action
senses.definitionCN: 继续进行某项活动、计划或行动方针
senses.example: The committee will pursue the investigation despite the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有延误，委员会仍将继续这项调查。
senses.why: 'To proceed, to follow (a path), usually figurative' is recorded from the late 14c., and the sense was already in Latin. Continuing is following without stopping: the route stays, you just keep walking it.
senses.whyCN: 「继续进行、沿着（一条路）走，通常为比喻用法」记录于 14 世纪后期，拉丁语已有此义。继续就是不停步地跟随：路线不变，你只管一直走。

senses.title: To sue: follow a case into court
senses.titleCN: 起诉：把案子一路跟进法庭
senses.definition: to take legal action over a claim or wrong, to follow a case through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 就某项请求或过错采取法律行动，把案子跟到法庭
senses.example: The tenant pursued the landlord for the return of the deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 房客起诉房东，要求退还押金。
senses.why: Legal English says pursue a claim much as it says prosecute: Latin prosequi already meant 'follow up, pursue' and gave both words. A lawsuit is a trail you follow to its end, and the court is where the trail stops.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语说 pursue a claim，与说 prosecute 同理：拉丁语 prosequi 本有「跟进、追究」义，两个词都由此而来。诉讼就是一条跟到底的路线，法庭是这条路线的终点。

senses.title: To accompany: follow as an escort
senses.titleCN: 追随、随行：作为随从跟在后头
senses.definition: to follow or accompany someone, especially in order to attend or escort them
senses.definitionCN: 跟随或陪伴某人，尤指为了随侍或护送
senses.example: A small guard pursued the king along the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一小队卫兵沿路跟随国王。
senses.why: Latin prosequi meant 'follow, accompany, attend; follow after, escort', a neutral sense of being behind someone. English kept mostly the aggressive and goal-seeking branches, but the escort sense survives in the Latin-shaped doubling with prosecute and in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prosequi 意为「跟随、陪伴、随侍；跟随、护送」，是「跟在某人后面」的中性义。英语主要保留了攻击性与求取的两支，但「随行」义仍活在 prosecute 等拉丁形同源词和正式文体里。

senses.title: To dig into: follow a question to its source
senses.titleCN: 探究：顺着问题一路挖到源头
senses.definition: to investigate or examine something further, following a line of inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 进一步调查或研究某事物，沿着一条探究线索走
senses.example: The researchers pursued the anomaly until they found its cause.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者一路追查这个异常现象，直到找到原因。
senses.why: An inquiry is a trail: each answer opens the next step. The 'follow' core makes pursue the natural verb for research, where you do not stop at the first clue but keep behind the question.
senses.whyCN: 探究是一条线索：每个答案都打开下一步。「跟随」这个核心让 pursue 成为研究中的自然动词：你不在第一条线索处停下，而是始终坠在问题后面。

senses.title: To court: chase a person, not a thing
senses.titleCN: 追求某人：追的不是事物，是人
senses.definition: to try persistently to win someone's romantic interest
senses.definitionCN: 坚持不懈地争取某人的爱慕
senses.example: He pursued her for months before she agreed to a coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 他追了她好几个月，她才答应喝杯咖啡。
senses.why: The modern romantic sense simply moves the chase from goals and suspects to people. The old hostility is gone, but the structure is identical: someone ahead, you behind, refusing to stop.
senses.whyCN: 现代「追求某人」只是把追逐的对象从目标、嫌疑人换成了人。旧的敌意消失了，结构却一模一样：她在前，你在后，不肯停。

senses.title: To walk a path: follow a route or policy
senses.titleCN: 遵循路径：沿着一条路或方针走
senses.definition: to follow a path, route, or policy, often figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 沿着一条道路、路线或方针前进，常为比喻用法
senses.example: The country pursued a policy of neutrality for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家奉行中立政策数十年。
senses.why: The literal 'follow a path' sense is old and was already figurative in Latin for a course of action. A policy is a road: pursue it and you stay on it, which is why the verb means both 'walk along' and 'carry out'.
senses.whyCN: 「沿着一条路走」的实指义很古老，在拉丁语里已用于比喻「行动方针」。政策就是一条路：pursue 它就是走在上面，所以这个词既表「沿着走」，也表「奉行」。

intro.en: Pursue is built from pro- 'forward' and sequi 'to follow'. Its history runs from Latin escorting, through French chasing, to English ambition, litigation, and research — one verb for every kind of following.
intro.cn: pursue 由 pro-「向前」与 sequi「跟随」构成。它的历史从拉丁语的「随行护送」，经法语的「追赶」，走到英语里的抱负、诉讼与研究——一个动词包揽了所有「跟随」。

items.en: Prosequi meant 'follow, accompany, attend; follow after, escort; follow up, pursue'. It is pro- 'forward' plus sequi 'to follow'. The deeper PIE root *sekw- 'to follow' is a reconstruction with no written record, so that layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: Prosequi 意为「跟随、陪伴、随侍；跟随、护送；跟进、追究」，由 pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成。更深的印欧语词根 *sekw-「跟随」是重构形式、没有书面记录，因此那一层标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Spoken Latin reshaped the verb into *prosequare, the form behind the French family. The exact date and region of this reshaping are not recorded, so the timing is source uncertain.
items.cn: 口语拉丁语把这个动词改造成 *prosequare，法语词族即由此而来。这一改造的确切年代与地区没有记录，因此时间标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Poursuir, with the variant porsivre, meant 'to chase, pursue, follow; continue, carry on'. The two strands English later separated — chasing and continuing — were already together in French.
items.cn: Poursuir（变体 porsivre）意为「追赶、追求、跟随；继续、进行」。英语后来分开的两条线——追捕与继续——在法语里已经并存。

items.en: Anglo-French pursuer and the English verb appear as 'follow with hostile intent, follow with a view of overtaking'. This is the hunting sense that still dominates police reports.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 pursuer 与英语动词出现时意为「带敌意跟随，意在赶上」。这就是至今主导警情报道的追捕义。

items.en: Two quieter senses join: 'to proceed, to follow (a path)', usually figurative for a course of action, and 'to seek, seek to obtain'. Both were already Latin, so English did not invent them; it simply kept more of the parent verb.
items.cn: 两个更安静的义项加入：「继续进行、沿着（一条路）走」（通常比喻行动方针）与「寻求、力求获得」。两者拉丁语已有，英语并非自创，只是保留了母词更多的义项。

items.en: Legal 'pursue a claim' follows the same 'follow it to the end' image, and the 20c. romantic 'pursue someone' moves the chase to people. No new source is involved: both are the old following verb applied to new objects.
items.cn: 法律用语 pursue a claim 沿用的是同一个「一路跟到底」的意象；20 世纪「追求某人」把追逐对象换成了人。两者都没有新词源，只是那个古老的「跟随」动词用在了新对象上。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the act of chasing or striving. It is the noun built on pursue, so the resemblance is real.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追求。它是 pursue 衍生出的名词，形似是真的。

entries.definition: done in accordance with something, as in pursuant to the rules. It keeps the French participle shape.

entries.definition: to read through carefully. It resembles pursue but comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 细读。它形似 pursue，但词源不同。

entries.definition: a small bag for money. It shares the opening pur- and nothing else.
entries.definitionCN: 钱包。它只与 pursue 共享开头的 pur-，别无关联。

entries.definition: to run after someone or something in order to catch it. It is the plain, physical word.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追逐。它是最朴素、最实指的对应词。

entries.definition: to go or come after someone. It lacks the urgency and hostility of pursue.
entries.definitionCN: 跟随。它没有 pursue 那种急迫与敌意。

entries.definition: to try to find or obtain something. It matches the goal sense but not the chasing.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找；寻求。它对应目标义，但不含追赶。

entries.definition: to conduct a legal case against someone. It is the Latin-shaped twin of pursue in law.
entries.definitionCN: 起诉；检控。它是 pursue 在法律领域的拉丁形姐妹词。

entries.definition: to chase game or search for something persistently. It stresses effort and prey.
entries.definitionCN: 打猎；搜寻。它强调用力与猎物。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin sequi 'to follow', prosequi 'follow after', and the English family pursuit, pursuant, prosecute.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 sequi「跟随」、prosequi「跟随、追究」，以及英语词族 pursuit、pursuant、prosecute。

normal.en: pursue = pro- 'forward' + sequi 'follow': follow forward, and keep following.
normal.cn: pursue = pro-「向前」+ sequi「跟随」：向前跟，而且跟到底。

normal.en: The same sequi gives sequence and consecutive: all of them are about one thing after another.
normal.cn: 同一个 sequi 给出 sequence、consecutive：它们讲的都是一个接一个。

normal.en: Pursue and prosecute are twins: the same Latin verb, one French-shaped, one Latin-shaped.
normal.cn: pursue 与 prosecute 是双胞胎：同一个拉丁动词，一个走法语形，一个走拉丁形。

normal.en: A pursuer is literally 'the one behind you', which is why the word works for detectives and suitors alike.
normal.cn: pursuer 字面上就是「你身后那个人」，所以它同时适用于侦探和求爱者。

normal.en: pursuant to the rules means following the rules, with the old participle still visible.
normal.cn: pursuant to the rules 意为「依据规则」，古老的现在分词仍看得见。

abstract.en: The core is relative position: the target ahead, the pursuer behind, the gap closing or held.
abstract.cn: 核心是相对位置：目标在前，追者在后，距离在缩短或保持。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps the same geometry; only the object changes: a deer, a degree, a lawsuit, a person.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保持同一种几何关系，只换对象：一头鹿、一个学位、一场官司、一个人。

abstract.en: To pursue is never to arrive instantly: the word lives in the interval.
abstract.cn: pursue 从来不是立刻抵达：这个词活在「还没追上」的那段时间里。

examples.en: She decided to pursue a doctorate in linguistics.
examples.cn: 她决定攻读语言学博士学位。

examples.en: The guards pursued the escaped prisoner across the field.
examples.cn: 看守们穿过田野追捕那名逃犯。

examples.en: The company may pursue legal action if the payments stop.
examples.cn: 如果付款停止，公司可能会提起诉讼。

dict_mnemonic.text: per（一直）+ sue（告）——一直跟着、一直告下去 → pursue 追赶、追求、起诉

root: 源自拉丁语 prosequi「跟随、随行、追究」，由 pro-「向前」+ sequi「跟随」构成；经法语 porsivre/poursuir 进入英语，核心始终是「跟在后面、一路不停」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one geometry: something is ahead of you and you keep after it. Whether it is a suspect, a career, an investigation, a policy, or a person, the verb never changes direction — only what is being followed.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一种几何关系：一样东西在你前面，你一路跟着。无论那是嫌疑人、职业、调查、政策还是一个人，这个动词的方向从不改变，变的只是被跟随的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: staying behind a moving target and refusing to let the gap open.
core.cn: 核心意象：始终坠在一个移动的目标后面，不让距离拉开。

branches.en: THE GOAL AHEAD: ambition, and the inquiry that follows a question to its source.
branches.cn: 前方的目标：抱负，以及顺着问题追到源头的探究。

branches.en: THE LIVING QUARRY: hunting a suspect, and courting a person.
branches.cn: 活的猎物：追捕嫌疑人，以及追求一个人。

branches.en: CARRYING ON: practising a profession, and continuing a course of action.
branches.cn: 持续进行：从事一门职业，以及继续一项行动。

branches.en: THE CASE: following a claim all the way into court.
branches.cn: 案子：把一项请求一路跟进法庭。

branches.en: THE PATH: escorting someone, and walking a route or policy.
branches.cn: 路径：随行护送某人，以及沿一条路线或方针前行。

intro.en: Pursue is pro- plus sequ- plus the French verb ending. Its family shows the prefix pro- 'forward', the root sequ- 'follow', and the suffixes -er, -ant, -ance, and -ing.
intro.cn: pursue 是 pro- 加 sequ- 再加法语动词词尾。它的词族展示前缀 pro-「向前」、词根 sequ-「跟随」，以及后缀 -er、-ant、-ance、-ing。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi 'to follow' is the base of prosequi 'follow after' and of the English words sequence, consecutive and prosecute. The French branch softened -sequ- into -su-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sequi「跟随」是 prosequi「跟随、追究」的基础，也是英语 sequence、consecutive、prosecute 的基础。法语一支把 -sequ- 软化成了 -su-。

definition_zh: 爆炸；爆发；激增
definition_en: a sudden violent burst; a sudden outbreak of strong emotion; a rapid increase

senses.exampleCN: 网购的激增改变了零售业。
senses.why: A burst becomes sudden growth.

normal.en: These are fundamental skills for reading.
normal.cn: 这些是阅读的基础技能。

normal.en: The course teaches the fundamentals of law.
normal.cn: 这门课教授法学基本原理。

normal.en: There is a fundamental difference between the two plans.

normal.en: Clean water is a fundamental right.

abstract.en: Fix the foundation before painting the wall.

abstract.en: Basics are boring only to those who skip them.
abstract.cn: 只有跳过基础的人才会觉得它无聊。

examples.en: Honesty is fundamental to trust.
examples.cn: 诚实是信任的根本基础。

examples.en: These are fundamental skills for reading.
examples.cn: 这些是阅读的基础技能。

examples.en: There is a fundamental difference between the two plans.

dict_mnemonic.text: fundamental = fundament（基础）+ -al（……的）；fundamentally 是「从根本上」，fundamentals 是「基本原理」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fundamentum（地基），由 fundare（奠定基础）而来；核心义「位于底层的、根本的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fundamental describes a base, a basic skill, or the basic rules of a subject.
sensesIntro.cn: fundamental 形容基础、基本技能，或一门学科的基本原理。

core.en: The base that holds everything else up.
core.cn: 支撑其他一切的基础。

branches.en: Trust rests on honesty.
branches.cn: 信任建立在诚实之上。

branches.en: Reading begins with basic skills.
branches.cn: 阅读从基本技能开始。

branches.en: Law study starts with its principles.
branches.cn: 法学学习从原理开始。

branches.en: What is basic supports what is advanced.
branches.cn: 基础支撑进阶。

branches.en: Skills and principles both begin at the base.
branches.cn: 技能与原理都始于基础。

intro.en: Fundamental builds words about foundations.
intro.cn: fundamental 构成与基础有关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base fundament- means foundation.

受教育是一项基本权利。
