There is a fundamental difference in aim.

definition_zh: 部长；大臣；牧师；公使
definition_en: a senior member of a government who heads a department, a religious leader who leads worship, or a diplomat ranked below an ambassador
core_image: 一个身着礼服的人站在门口，手里捧着别人交办的文件
scene: 议会走廊里，记者们围住一位刚走出会议室的人，等他开口谈预算。 The minister answered questions for nearly an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 minister 是「部长」（第 1 个义项：主管政府部门的资深政客）；句意为部长回答了将近一小时的提问。画面里可抓住的物件：议会走廊、会议室门、录音笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 minister 加 -ial 构成，义为「部长的；大臣的；牧师的」
由 minister 加 -y 构成，义为「部；内阁部门；神职」
由拉丁 ministrare 加 -ation 构成，义为「服侍；宗教仪式」
由拉丁 ad- 加 ministrare 构成，义为「管理；施行」

senses.title: A head of a government department
senses.definition: a senior politician who is in charge of a government department
senses.definitionCN: 主管某一个政府部门的资深政界人物
senses.example: The finance minister resigned after the budget vote.
senses.exampleCN: 预算表决之后，财政部长辞职了。
senses.why: Latin minister first meant a servant or attendant; a person who served the crown at the head of an office grew into the modern sense of a senior state official.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minister 最初指仆人、随从；在朝廷里替君主办事、主管一个衙门的人，逐渐长成现代「政府部长」的意思。

senses.title: A religious leader of a congregation
senses.definition: a person ordained to lead worship and care for a congregation, especially in Protestant churches
senses.definitionCN: 受按立以主持礼拜、照看会众的人，尤指新教教会的牧师
senses.example: The minister read the names of the dead aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师大声念出逝者的名字。
senses.why: The same word for a servant was used in the church for one who serves the congregation; the religious sense is older in English than the political one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「仆人」的词在教会里指服侍会众的人；在英语里，宗教义比政治义出现得更早。

senses.title: A diplomat below an ambassador
senses.definition: a diplomatic representative of a country, ranking below an ambassador and above lower embassy staff
senses.definitionCN: 一国派出的外交代表，地位低于大使、高于使馆较低级别的职员
senses.example: She was posted to the embassy as minister for trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她被派往使馆担任贸易公使。
senses.why: Diplomacy borrowed the ranking vocabulary of courts: a minister served a sovereign abroad, and the title stayed for envoys who rank just under an ambassador.
senses.whyCN: 外交沿用宫廷的等级词汇：minister 曾在国外替君主办事，这个头衔便留给地位略低于大使的使节。

intro.en: Minister goes back to a Latin word for a servant, and its journey from household attendant to cabinet member and clergy explains why one word covers three jobs.
intro.cn: minister 可追到拉丁语中表示仆人的词；它从家仆走到内阁成员与神职人员，这条路径解释了一个词为何能涵盖三种职务。

items.en: Minus meant less, and from it Latin built words for people or things that stood lower in a hierarchy.
items.cn: minus 意为较少、较低；拉丁语由它造出表示在等级中位置较低的人或事物的词。

items.en: Minister named an attendant, a servant or an agent who acted for someone else, including an assistant in religious rites.
items.cn: minister 指随从、仆人或替别人办事的代理人，也包括宗教仪式中的助手。

items.en: The verb ministrare meant to serve, to attend or to manage, and it produced a whole family of English words such as administer.
items.cn: 动词 ministrare 意为服侍、随侍或经办，由此产生 administer 等一整族英语词。

items.en: Old French took the noun as menistre, a servant or an official, and carried it into English after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 menistre，指仆人或官员，诺曼征服之后传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps minister for a cabinet member, a clergyperson and a mid-ranked diplomat, while ministry splits off as the office itself.
items.cn: 现代英语用 minister 指内阁成员、神职人员与中等层级的外交官，而 ministry 则分出去指职务机构本身。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin stem of service; the near-meaning group collects other titles for officials, clergy and envoys.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「服务」词干上的词；近义组收官员、神职人员与使节的其他称谓。

entries.definition: A government department, the cabinet, or the office of a religious minister.
entries.definitionCN: 政府部门、内阁，或牧师的职务。

entries.definition: Relating to a minister, a government department or a pastor's duties.
entries.definitionCN: 与部长、政府部门或牧师职责有关的。

entries.definition: To manage an organization or to give a treatment or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 管理一个机构，或施行某种治疗、执行某项规则。

entries.definition: The act of serving or helping, often in a religious setting.
entries.definitionCN: 服侍、帮助的行为，常用于宗教场合。

entries.definition: A senior government official who heads a department in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 美国联邦政府中主管一个部门的资深官员。

entries.definition: A minister in charge of a church and its congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 主管一间教堂及其会众的牧师。

entries.definition: A diplomat sent to represent a country, usually ranking below an ambassador.
entries.definitionCN: 被派往代表一国的外交官，通常地位低于大使。

entries.definition: A person who holds a position of authority in a government or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 在政府或机构中担任有权威职位的人。

normalIntro.en: The word began as Latin for a servant, and every modern sense still keeps a trace of someone acting on another's behalf.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是拉丁语中的「仆人」，每个现代义项都还留着「替别人办事」的痕迹。

normal.en: Latin minister meant servant or attendant, which is why the word fits both a cabinet member serving the state and a pastor serving a congregation.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 minister 意为仆人或随从，所以这个词既适合替国家办事的内阁成员，也适合服侍会众的牧师。

normal.en: Ministrare is the verb behind administer, so minister and administer are siblings rather than unrelated words.
normal.cn: ministrare 是 administer 背后的动词，所以 minister 与 administer 是同胞词，而非互不相干的词。

normal.en: Ministry is the office, minister is the person: the -y ending names the institution, the bare word names the human being.
normal.cn: ministry 是机构，minister 是人：-y 词尾命名制度，光秃秃的词干则指具体的人。

normal.en: Prime minister is a fixed phrase, and the stress falls on the first word, so it sounds like one title rather than two.
normal.cn: prime minister 是固定说法，重音落在第一个词上，所以听起来像一个头衔而不是两个词。

normal.en: The diplomatic rank is the oldest of the three modern uses in court language, because an envoy was literally a servant sent abroad.
normal.cn: 三个现代义项里，外交级别在宫廷用语中出现得最早，因为使节字面上就是被派往国外的仆人。

abstract.en: Picture a servant holding a sealed letter at a palace door: the same figure becomes a cabinet member and a pastor.
abstract.cn: 想象一个仆人站在宫门口，手里拿着一封封好的信：同一个人物后来变成了内阁成员与牧师。

abstract.en: A minister never acts alone; the word always points to someone who works for another party.
abstract.cn: minister 从不单独行动；这个词始终指向替另一方办事的人。

abstract.en: One Latin noun for service splits into a person, an office and a rank, like a single trunk with three branches.
abstract.cn: 一个表示服务的拉丁名词分成一个人、一个机构与一个级别，像一根主干长出三根枝条。

examples.en: The finance minister resigned after the budget vote.
examples.cn: 预算表决之后，财政部长辞职了。

examples.en: The minister read the names of the dead aloud.
examples.cn: 牧师大声念出逝者的名字。

examples.en: She was posted to the embassy as minister for trade.
examples.cn: 她被派往使馆担任贸易公使。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你斯特」——听上去像「迷你」的随从，职位再高也是替国家办事的仆从；minister 是部长、大臣。

root: 拉丁语 minister（仆人、随从）一般认为由 minus（较少、较低）加比较级后缀构成，义为「地位较低者」；动词 ministrare（服侍、经办）派生 administer 等词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is service on behalf of another; the senses divide into the head of a department, the leader of a congregation, and a diplomatic rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是替他人服务；各义项分成主管部门的首长、会众的属灵领袖，以及一个外交级别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a servant in formal dress standing at a door, holding papers handed over by someone else.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个穿礼服的仆人站在门口，手里捧着别人交办的文件。

branches.en: a politician leaving a cabinet room under a wall of cameras
branches.cn: 在镜头包围下走出内阁会议室的政客

branches.en: a pastor reading names from a pulpit
branches.cn: 在讲坛上念名字的牧师

branches.en: an envoy handing over papers in a foreign capital
branches.cn: 在异国首都递交文件的使节

branches.en: one title shared by a cabinet post and a diplomatic rank
branches.cn: 同一个头衔既指内阁职位又指外交级别

branches.en: a figure who speaks for a community abroad or before a congregation
branches.cn: 在海外或会众面前代表群体说话的人

intro.en: Minister is a Latin noun of service, backed by a verb of serving and by the suffix that turns it into an office.
intro.cn: minister 是表示服务的拉丁名词，背后有一个表示服侍的动词，以及把它变成机构名的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is a Latin noun of service, and the same stem reappears in ministry, administer and ministerial.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是表示「服务」的拉丁名词，同一词干又出现在 ministry、administer 与 ministerial 中。

definition_zh: 肉；肉体；果肉
definition_en: the soft tissue of a body, the edible part of an animal, or the soft part of a fruit
core_image: 刀切下去，露出湿润的粉色肌理
scene: 刀切开了果肉。 The knife cut through the flesh of the fruit.
sceneCN: 这里 flesh 是「果肉」（第 2 个义项）；句意：刀切开了果肉。

senses.title: Body tissue
senses.definition: the soft part of a body between skin and bone
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤与骨骼之间的柔软部分
senses.example: The wound went deep into the flesh.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口深深进了肉里。
senses.why: This is the basic anatomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的解剖学义项。

senses.title: Fruit pulp
senses.definition: the soft edible part of a fruit
senses.definitionCN: 水果柔软可食的部分
senses.example: The knife cut through the flesh of the fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 刀切开了果肉。
senses.why: The soft body of a fruit resembles soft body tissue.
senses.whyCN: 水果柔软的部分类似柔软的身体组织。

senses.title: Physical body
senses.definition: the body as opposed to the spirit or mind
senses.definitionCN: 相对于精神或心灵的肉身
senses.example: The story speaks of the spirit and the flesh.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事谈论灵魂与肉体。
senses.why: Flesh came to stand for human physical nature.
senses.whyCN: flesh 进而代表人的肉体天性。

senses.title: To add detail
senses.definition: to add details to make an idea complete
senses.definitionCN: 添加细节使想法变得完整
senses.example: She fleshed out the plan with numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 她用数据充实了这个计划。
senses.why: Giving a plan flesh is giving it body.
senses.whyCN: 给计划加上「肉」就是让它有实体。

intro.en: Flesh is an old Germanic word, Old English flæsc, unchanged in meaning at its core.
intro.cn: flesh 是古老的日耳曼语词，古英语作 flæsc，核心含义几乎未变。

items.en: Flaiska named the soft parts of the body.
items.cn: flaiska 指身体柔软的部分。

items.en: Flæsc meant flesh or meat.
items.cn: flæsc 意为肉或肌肉。

items.en: Flesh kept both body and food senses.
items.cn: flesh 同时保留身体与食物两义。

items.en: The word named the soft part of fruit.
items.cn: 这个词开始指水果柔软的部分。

items.en: Flesh out became an idiom for adding detail.
items.cn: flesh out 成为「充实细节」的习语。

note.en: Flesh is compared with similar-looking words and with words for meat and pulp.
note.cn: 把 flesh 与形近词以及表示肉和果肉的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sudden burst of light
entries.definitionCN: 闪光

entries.definition: new or recently made
entries.definitionCN: 新鲜的

entries.definition: to become red
entries.definitionCN: 脸红

entries.definition: animal flesh used as food
entries.definitionCN: 食用肉

entries.definition: tissue that moves the body
entries.definitionCN: 肌肉

entries.definition: the soft wet part of fruit
entries.definitionCN: 果肉

normalIntro.en: Flesh is the soft living middle: of a body, of a fruit, of a plan that needs detail.
normalIntro.cn: flesh 是柔软的生命中层：身体的、水果的、以及需要细节的计划。

normal.en: The flesh of the peach is sweet.
normal.cn: 桃子的果肉很甜。

normal.en: The thorn cut into his flesh.
normal.cn: 刺划进了他的肉里。

normal.en: They met him in the flesh.
normal.cn: 他们见到了他本人。

normal.en: Flesh out the idea with examples.
normal.cn: 用例子充实这个想法。

normal.en: Flesh and blood ties the family together.
normal.cn: 血缘把家庭连在一起。

abstract.en: The soft part is where life is felt.
abstract.cn: 柔软之处正是生命被感知的地方。

abstract.en: To give flesh to an idea is to make it visible.
abstract.cn: 给想法以血肉就是让它可见。

abstract.en: Body and spirit argue in one word.
abstract.cn: 身体与精神在同一个词里争论。

examples.en: The knife cut through the flesh of the fruit.
examples.cn: 刀切开了果肉。

examples.en: The wound went deep into the flesh.
examples.cn: 伤口深深进了肉里。

examples.en: She fleshed out the plan with numbers.
examples.cn: 她用数据充实了这个计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: flesh 源自古英语 flæsc（肉），核心义「身体柔软的部分」，再引申为果肉与「充实细节」。

root: 源自古英语 flæsc（肉），核心义「身体柔软的组织」。

sensesIntro.en: Flesh means body tissue, edible meat, fruit pulp, the physical body, or to add detail.
sensesIntro.cn: flesh 意为身体组织、食用肉、果肉、肉体，或充实细节。

core.en: The soft living part of a body.
core.cn: 身体柔软而有生命的部分。

branches.en: Soft tissue under the skin.
branches.cn: 皮肤下的柔软组织。

branches.en: The soft edible part of fruit.
branches.cn: 水果柔软可食的部分。

branches.en: The body seen against the spirit.
branches.cn: 相对于精神的肉身。

branches.en: Detail that gives an idea body.
branches.cn: 让想法有实体的细节。

branches.en: Body tissue and fruit pulp share softness.
branches.cn: 身体组织与果肉共享柔软。

intro.en: Flesh builds words for texture, body, and the lack of both.
intro.cn: flesh 构成表示质地、肉体以及二者缺失的词。

latinIntro.en: Flesh has no Latin ancestor; Latin caro, flesh, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flesh 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 caro（肉）只是语义对应词。

items.example: Fleshing out the report took a week.

items.exampleCN: 这种植物有肥厚的叶子。

items.example: The fruit is known for fleshiness.
items.exampleCN: 这种水果以果肉厚著称。

definition_zh: 地区；区域；地带；行政区；领域；（身体的）部位；（数值的）大约范围
definition_en: a broad area of land or space, an administrative division, a field of activity, or an approximate range
core_image: 一条线在地上画出的圈：圈内是一片地，圈外是别的世界
scene: 火车穿过山口之后，窗外的语言、屋顶和葡萄品种都变了。 The conductor said that they had entered another region, where the roofs and the grapes looked nothing like the ones at home.
sceneCN: 这里 region 是「地理区域」（第 2 个义项：世界或国土的一部分）；句意：列车员说他们已经进入另一个区域，那里的屋顶和葡萄都跟家乡完全不一样。场景要点：山口隧道、车窗外变换的屋顶样式、葡萄园、站牌上的地名。

pos.zh: 地区；区域；行政区；领域；部位

derivatives.zh: 地区的；区域性的；地方性的

senses.title: A broad tract of land
senses.definition: a broad area of land whose boundaries are not precisely fixed
senses.definitionCN: 一大片土地，其边界并不精确固定
senses.example: The northern region is mostly forest and thin soil.
senses.exampleCN: 北部地区主要是森林和贫瘠的土壤。
senses.why: Latin regio came from regere 'to direct, rule', and originally named a line or boundary. A region is land that has been marked off, even if the mark is only approximate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regio 来自 regere“引导、统治”，最初指一条线或边界。region 就是被划出来的一片地，即使那条线只是大致的。

senses.title: A part of the world
senses.definition: a part of the world or of a country, usually identified by climate, culture, or position
senses.definitionCN: 世界或国家的一个部分，通常以气候、文化或位置来识别
senses.example: Coffee grows best in tropical regions with steady rain.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在雨水稳定的热带地区长得最好。
senses.why: The bounded tract is scaled up to the map. Once the line is drawn on a map, the land inside is a region, and neighbouring regions acquire different climates and customs.
senses.whyCN: 被划出的地块放大到了地图上。一旦线被画在地图上，圈内的土地就是一个 region，相邻的区域也获得了不同的气候与习俗。

senses.title: An administrative division
senses.definition: a named administrative division of a country, with its own government or offices
senses.definitionCN: 国家的一个有名行政区划，拥有自己的政府或机构
senses.example: The region of Campania has its own governor and budget.
senses.exampleCN: 坎帕尼亚大区有自己的行政长官和预算。
senses.why: Here the boundary is legal rather than natural. The line is drawn by an authority, which is exactly what the root regere 'to rule' implies: the ruler's line makes the region.
senses.whyCN: 这里的边界是法律的，而不是自然的。线由权威画出，这正是词根 regere“统治”所暗示的：统治者的线造出了区域。

senses.title: The countryside around a city
senses.definition: the rural area lying around a city, used in contrast with the city itself
senses.definitionCN: 环绕城市的那片乡村地带，与城市本身相对
senses.example: The old nobility still owned estates in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 旧贵族仍在这一带拥有庄园。
senses.why: From the late 14th century the word also named the land outside the walls. The city is the centre, and the region is the ring of fields and villages around it.
senses.whyCN: 从 14 世纪晚期起，这个词也指城墙之外的土地。城市是中心，region 就是环绕它的那一圈田野与村庄。

senses.title: A part of the body
senses.definition: a defined part or zone of the body, especially in anatomy and medicine
senses.definitionCN: 身体的一个确定部位或区域，尤用于解剖学与医学
senses.example: The surgeon worked on the lumbar region of the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在脊柱的腰部区域动手术。
senses.why: The line that marks off land is redrawn on the body. Anatomy divides the body into named regions, so the same word for a bounded tract now names a bounded part.
senses.whyCN: 划出土地的那条线被重新画在身体上。解剖学把身体分成有名字的区域，于是同一个表示“被划出的地块”的词，现在命名一个被划出的部位。

senses.title: A sphere of activity or thought
senses.definition: a field of activity, knowledge, or thought with its own boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或思想的一个领域，有自己的边界
senses.example: That question lies outside the region of physics.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题落在物理学的领域之外。
senses.why: The boundary becomes invisible. What separates physics from poetry is not a fence but a limit of method, yet the mind still pictures a territory with an inside and an outside.
senses.whyCN: 边界变得看不见了。把物理学与诗歌分开的不是篱笆，而是方法的界限，但头脑仍然把它想象成一块有内有外的领地。

senses.title: An approximate range of a number
senses.definition: in the phrase in the region of, approximately or about a particular amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in the region of 这一短语，表示大约、在某个数量左右
senses.example: The repairs will cost in the region of ten thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 维修费用大约在一万英镑左右。
senses.why: The bounded area becomes a bounded interval on a scale. A number 'in the region of' ten thousand is not exactly ten thousand; it is somewhere inside that neighbourhood.
senses.whyCN: 「某一范围」也可以表示大约的数量：介于两个界限之间，就像一大片区域围出的空间，引申为「约数」。英语里 in the region of 就是这个用法。

senses.title: A layer or zone of the atmosphere
senses.definition: one of the horizontal layers or zones of the atmosphere, oceans, or space
senses.definitionCN: 大气、海洋或空间中水平划分的一层或一个带
senses.example: Weather balloons climb into the upper region of the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 气象气球升入大气的高层区域。
senses.why: Height is divided into horizontal bands the way land is divided into tracts. The upper region is not a place with a fence but a layer with a defined range.
senses.whyCN: 高度像土地被分成地块那样，被分成水平的带。高层区域不是有篱笆的地方，而是一个有确定范围的一层。

senses.title: A bounded area in computing
senses.titleCN: 计算机中的一个限定区域
senses.definition: a defined block of memory, or a selected area of a screen or map
senses.definitionCN: 一块被限定的内存区域，或屏幕、地图上被选定的区域
senses.example: The program copies the image into a separate memory region.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把图像复制到一个单独的内存区域。
senses.why: Software needs edges even when nothing physical is being divided. A memory region is a range with a start and an end, the same bounded tract expressed as two addresses.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有实体被分割，软件也需要边界。内存区域是一段有起点和终点的范围，也就是同一块被限定的地，用两个地址表达出来。

intro.en: Region looks as if it begins with re-, but it does not: the re- belongs to the root reg-, from Latin regere 'to direct, rule'. The word's core is a line drawn to bound a tract of land. That makes region unlike recover (capere 'take'), require (quaerere 'ask'), research (circare 'go about') and reside (sedere 'sit'), all of which carry a real re- prefix.
intro.cn: region 看起来像以 re- 开头，其实不是：它的 re- 属于词根 reg-，来自拉丁语 regere“引导、统治”。这个词的核心是一条画出来、把一片地围住的线。因此 region 与 recover（capere“拿取”）、require（quaerere“询问”）、research（circare“绕行”）、reside（sedere“坐”）都不同，后四个才带真正的前缀 re-。

items.en: First recorded as regioun, 'tract of land of a considerable but indefinite extent'. It also meant 'a kingdom, country, nation; the people of a country'.
items.cn: 最早记录为 regioun，意为“范围相当大但边界不定的一片土地”，同时也表示“王国、国家、民族；一国的人民”。

items.en: From Anglo-French regioun and Old French region 'land, region, province' (12c.), and directly from Latin regionem, nominative regio.
items.cn: 来自盎格鲁法语 regioun 与古法语 region“土地、地区、省份”（12 世纪），并直接来自拉丁语 regionem（主格 regio）。

items.en: Latin regio meant 'a district, portion of a country, territory; a direction, line; boundary line, limit'. It was a noun of state from the past-participle stem of regere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 regio 意为“区、国家的一部分、领土；方向、直线；边界线、界限”。它是 regere 过去分词词干的性状名词。

items.en: Regere means 'to direct, rule', from PIE *reg- 'move in a straight line', with derivatives meaning 'to direct in a straight line', hence 'to lead, rule'. A straight line is what makes a boundary.
items.cn: regere 意为“引导、统治”，来自原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动”，其派生义为“沿直线引导”，进而表示“带领、统治”。正是直线构成了边界。

items.en: The sense 'a part of the world' appears in the late 14th century, as does 'the rural area around a city'. The word is now both a map unit and a city's hinterland.
items.cn: “世界的一个部分”这一义项出现于 14 世纪晚期，“城市周边的乡村地带”也在同一时期出现。这个词如今既是地图单位，也是城市腹地。

items.en: The phrase in the region of 'about' is recorded from 1961. Regional is from the early 15th century, and subregion from 1830. The Latin root also gives regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle.
items.cn: 短语 in the region of“大约”记录于 1961 年。regional 始于 15 世纪早期，subregion 始于 1830 年。同一拉丁词根还给出 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle。

note.en: The first group separates the derived forms from the noun; the second compares the four area words learners mix up. Region is usually a large or officially bounded area, while its re- is part of reg- 'rule', not the prefix of recover, require, research or reside.
note.cn: 第一组把派生形式同名词分开；第二组比较学习者容易混用的四个“区域”词。region 通常指较大或官方划定的区域，而它的 re- 属于 reg-“统治”，不是 recover、require、research、reside 的那个前缀。

entries.definition: relating to a particular region. It describes something belonging to a region, while region names the area itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一地区有关的。它描述属于某个地区的事物，而 region 命名这个地区本身。

entries.definition: loyalty to one's own region, or a feature peculiar to it. It is an attitude or a local trait, not the area.
entries.definitionCN: 对本地区的忠诚，或本地区特有的特征。它是一种态度或地方特色，而不是地区本身。

entries.definition: in a regional way or at the regional level. It modifies an action, while region is a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以地区方式，或在地区层面上。它修饰动作，而 region 是名词。

entries.definition: a smaller division inside a region. The sub- marks a region within a region.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区内部的更小分区。sub- 标记“区域之中的区域”。

entries.definition: a part of a place or a measured surface. It is the most general word and can be as small as a room; region usually suggests a larger or more defined stretch.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的一部分，或一个被测量的表面。它是最通用的词，可以小到一个房间；region 通常暗示更大或更明确的一片。

entries.definition: an official division of a city, country, or organization for administration. It is usually smaller and more precisely defined than a region.
entries.definitionCN: 城市、国家或组织为行政而划分的正式区域。它通常比 region 更小、边界更精确。

entries.definition: an area marked off for a particular purpose, such as a climate zone or a no-parking zone. It stresses function or rule, while region stresses land or extent.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的划出的区域，如气候带或禁停区。它强调功能或规则，而 region 强调土地或范围。

entries.definition: a kingdom, or a sphere of activity. It is more literary and more abstract than region, and it comes from a different French source, not from the Latin reg- root.
entries.definitionCN: 王国，或活动的领域。它比 region 更文学化、更抽象，而且来自另一条法语来源，并非拉丁语 reg- 词根。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regere 'to rule, direct', regio 'a bounded district', the *reg- family, and the five derived forms regional, regionally, regionalism, regionalize and subregion.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regere“统治、引导”、regio“被划定的区”、*reg- 词族，以及五个派生形式 regional、regionally、regionalism、regionalize、subregion。

normal.en: regere means 'to rule, direct', and a ruler draws straight lines. A region is the land inside one of those lines.
normal.cn: regere 意为“统治、引导”，而统治者画直线。region 就是其中一条线以内的土地。

normal.en: The same *reg- root gives regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle — all about straight lines and rule.
normal.cn: 同一 *reg- 词根给出 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle——全都关于直线与统治。

normal.en: Region's re- is not a prefix: it is the start of reg-, so do not link it to recover or reside.
normal.cn: region 的 re- 不是前缀：它是 reg- 的开头，所以不要把它和 recover 或 reside 联系起来。

normal.en: in the region of means 'about': a number inside a small neighbourhood on a scale.
normal.cn: in the region of 意为“大约”：刻度上某个数附近的一小片邻域。

normal.en: Regional is the adjective, regionalism the attitude, and subregion a region inside a region.
normal.cn: regional 是形容词，regionalism 是态度，subregion 是区域内部的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler drawing one straight line across a map. Everything on one side becomes a region; everything on the other side becomes somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子在地图上画下一条直线。线这一侧的一切成为一个 region；另一侧的一切成为别处。

abstract.en: The line can be moved from land to the body, to thought, to numbers, to memory: wherever a boundary is drawn, there is a region inside it.
abstract.cn: 这条线可以从土地移到身体、思想、数字与内存：只要画下一条边界，界内就有一个 region。

abstract.en: A region is not the line itself but the inside it creates, which is why the word always implies both an edge and a stretch of ground.
abstract.cn: region 不是线本身，而是线所造成的内部，所以这个词总同时暗示一条边和一片地。

examples.en: The wine is grown in a cool region near the coast.
examples.cn: 这种葡萄酒产自沿海一个凉爽的地区。

examples.en: Damage to that region of the brain can affect speech.
examples.cn: 大脑那个区域受损可能影响言语能力。

examples.en: A new laptop will cost in the region of eight hundred dollars.
examples.cn: 一台新笔记本电脑大约要八百美元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞金」——瑞金既是一座城，也是一片有名的地区 → region 地区；区域（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regio“被划定的区”，其词根 regere 意为“引导、统治”，可追溯到原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动”，核心是“用一条线划出来的一片地”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of region, all from one act: drawing a line to bound a stretch. The stretch can be land, a part of the world, a province, a city's hinterland, a body part, a field of thought, a numeric neighbourhood, a layer of air, or a block of memory.
sensesIntro.cn: region 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：画一条线，把一片范围围起来。这片范围可以是土地、世界的一部分、省份、城市腹地、身体部位、思想领域、数值邻域、大气的一层，或一块内存。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn to enclose a stretch of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：画下一条直线，把一片地圈在里面。

branches.en: LAND: an indefinite tract, a part of the world, and an administrative province are the same enclosed ground at three scales.
branches.cn: 土地：边界不定的一片地、世界的一部分、行政区划，是同一片被圈起来的土地在三种尺度上。

branches.en: AROUND THE CITY: the line is drawn at the city wall, and the fields outside become the region.
branches.cn: 城市周边：线画在城墙处，墙外的田野就成了 region。

branches.en: THE BODY: anatomy redraws the line inside a person and names the enclosed part.
branches.cn: 身体：解剖学把线画进人体内部，并给被围住的部位命名。

branches.en: THOUGHT: the boundary becomes invisible, marking what a discipline does and does not cover.
branches.cn: 思想：边界变得看不见，标记一门学科涵盖与不涵盖的范围。

branches.en: MEASURED RANGES: a numeric neighbourhood, a layer of atmosphere, and a block of memory are all bounded intervals rather than ground.
branches.cn: 可测的范围：数值邻域、大气的一层、一块内存，都是有界的区间，而不是土地。

intro.en: Region is not re- plus a root; it is the Latin stem reg- plus -ion. English adds -al, -ly, -ism, -ize and sub-. The same reg- root also supplies regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle.
intro.cn: region 不是 re- 加词根，而是拉丁词干 reg- 加 -ion。英语再加 -al、-ly、-ism、-ize 与 sub-。同一 reg- 词根还供应 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle。

latinIntro.en: Latin regere 'to direct, rule' gives the noun regio 'a district, boundary line', the noun rex 'king', and the noun regula 'rule, straight stick'. The PIE root *reg- means 'move in a straight line', which links ruling to drawing a straight boundary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regere“引导、统治”给出名词 regio“区、边界线”、名词 rex“国王”与名词 regula“规则、直尺”。原始印欧语词根 *reg- 意为“沿直线移动”，把“统治”与“画一条笔直的边界”联系起来。

items.meaning: a district bounded by a line
items.meaningCN: 被一条线划定的区域（reg- 引导 + -ion 状态名词）
items.example: The region has been famous for its wool for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区几百年来以羊毛闻名。

items.meaningCN: 地区的；区域性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Regional differences in accent are still strong.
items.exampleCN: 口音的地区差异仍然很明显。

items.meaning: at the level of a region
items.meaningCN: 在地区层面上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The paper is published regionally, not nationally.
items.exampleCN: 这份报纸在地区发行，而不是全国发行。

items.meaning: loyalty to a region, or a local feature
items.meaningCN: 地方主义；地方特色（-ism 构成主义或特征）
items.example: The novel is full of the regionalism of the northern coast.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说充满北部海岸的地方特色。

items.meaningCN: 按地区组织；使区域化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The company regionalized its supply chain last year.
items.exampleCN: 公司去年把供应链按地区重新组织。

items.meaning: a smaller division within a region
items.meaningCN: 亚区；分区（sub- 在下 + region）
items.example: Each subregion has a different rainfall pattern.
items.exampleCN: 每个分区都有不同的降雨模式。

items.meaning: belonging to a king or queen
items.meaningCN: 王室的；帝王般的（reg- 王 + -al 形容词）
items.example: The hall was decorated in regal red and gold.
items.exampleCN: 大厅以帝王般的红金两色装饰。

items.meaning: a person who rules during a monarch's absence or minority
items.meaningCN: 摄政者（reg- 统治 + -ent 行为者）
items.example: A regent governed the country while the king was abroad.
items.exampleCN: 国王出国期间由一位摄政者治理国家。

items.meaningCN: 管理；调节（regula 规则、直尺 + -ate 动词）
items.example: The agency regulates the safety of new drugs.
items.exampleCN: 该机构监管新药的安全。

items.meaningCN: 指导；导演（dis- + regere 使变直）
items.example: She directed the whole production herself.
items.exampleCN: 整场制作由她亲自执导。

items.meaningCN: 改正；正确的（com- 共同 + regere 使直）
items.example: He corrected the spelling on the label.
items.exampleCN: 他改正了标签上的拼写。

items.meaning: a four-sided shape with right angles
items.meaningCN: 长方形；矩形（rect- 直 + angle 角）
items.example: The garden is laid out as a long rectangle.
items.exampleCN: 花园被布置成一个狭长的矩形。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb, from PIE *reg- 'move in a straight line'

definition_zh: 品脱（容量单位）；一品脱装的东西（尤指啤酒）
definition_en: a unit of liquid measure equal to about half a litre, or the amount that a container of this size holds
core_image: 酒馆吧台上那杯带泡沫的大杯啤酒，正好装满一个标准杯
scene: 下班后他走进街角酒馆，要了一大杯冒泡的啤酒。 The barman pulled a perfect pint and set it on the counter.
sceneCN: 这里是「一品脱装的东西」（第 2 个义项：一品脱容量的杯中之物）；句意为酒保打出满满一品脱啤酒放在吧台上。画面就是那只标准的大啤酒杯。

derivatives.zh: pint 与 size 合成，义为「小号的；矮小的」，常带玩笑口吻
pint 与 glass 合成，义为「一品脱杯；标准啤酒杯」

senses.title: A unit of liquid volume
senses.definition: a measure of liquid volume equal to eight fluid ounces in the US or about 568 millilitres in the UK
senses.definitionCN: 液量单位，美制约四百七十多毫升，英制约五百六十八毫升
senses.example: The recipe calls for a pint of cream.
senses.exampleCN: 这道菜谱需要一品脱奶油。
senses.why: The old measure was carved on the ale quarts of medieval taverns, and the word kept its official size down the centuries.
senses.whyCN: 这个量制中世纪就刻在酒馆的酒量具上，几个世纪下来词保住了它官方的容量。

senses.title: A glass of beer
senses.definition: a glass of beer served in a container that holds one pint
senses.definitionCN: 装在一品脱容器里的啤酒
senses.example: He bought two pints and found a table by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了两杯啤酒，找了个靠窗的位子。
senses.why: In British pubs the standard beer glass is exactly a pint, so the measure became the drink itself.
senses.whyCN: 英式酒馆的标准啤酒杯正好一品脱，于是量词变成了酒本身。

senses.title: A container of that size
senses.definition: a bottle or carton that holds one pint of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 能装一品脱液体的瓶或盒
senses.example: She opened a pint of ice cream after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她开了一品脱装的冰淇淋。
senses.why: Milk and ice cream are sold in pint containers, so the word points to the package as well as the amount.
senses.whyCN: 牛奶和冰淇淋按品脱盒卖，这个词便既指分量也指包装。

senses.title: The pint measure in idioms
senses.definition: the idea of small size carried by compounds built on pint
senses.definitionCN: 由 pint 构成的复合词所带的小尺寸意味
senses.example: The pint-size guard was the fastest player on the court.
senses.exampleCN: 那个小个子后卫是球场上最快的球员。
senses.why: A single pint is a modest amount, so compounds borrow it to tease someone about being small.
senses.whyCN: 一品脱不算多，复合词便借它来打趣个子小。

intro.en: Pint goes back through Old French to a mark painted on a measuring vessel, so the word is literally a sign that was painted.
intro.cn: pint 经古法语追溯到一个画在量具上的记号，这个词的字面义就是一道画上去的标记。

items.en: Reconstructed *pincta is taken as the feminine past participle of pinctus, meaning painted or marked.
items.cn: 一般认为源自通俗拉丁语重构形式 *pincta，是 pinctus（涂画的）的阴性形式。

items.en: The verb pingere, to paint, underlies the reconstruction; marks on jugs showed how much they held.
items.cn: 动词 pingere（画）是重构形式的来源；罐子上的记号标示容量。

items.en: Old French pinte named both the measure and the marked vessel.
items.cn: 古法语 pinte 既指这个量制，也指带记号的容器。

items.en: The word entered English in the fourteenth century as an official liquid measure.
items.cn: 十四世纪该词进入英语，成为官方液量单位。

items.en: British pub culture fixed the pint glass as the shape of beer, making the measure a drink in daily speech.
items.cn: 英式酒馆文化把品脱杯定型为啤酒的形状，让量词在口语里变成了酒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share pint's sound or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers liquid measures.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pint 音形相近的词；近义组收液量单位。

entries.definition: A horse with patches of two colours; only the sound resembles pint.
entries.definitionCN: 花斑马；与 pint 只是读音相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: A sharp tip or an idea; spelled one letter differently from pint.
entries.definitionCN: 尖端或论点；拼写与 pint 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: Letters or images on paper; shares p-i-n-t letters in a different order.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷的文字图像；字母构成相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Two pints; the older tavern measure from which quart is named.
entries.definitionCN: 两品脱；词源即旧时酒馆的量制。

entries.definition: Eight pints in the imperial system.
entries.definitionCN: 英制中等于八品脱。

entries.definition: The metric unit that replaced pints in most of the world.
entries.definitionCN: 取代品脱的公制单位。

normalIntro.en: A short word of one syllable; memory works on the pub glass and on the painted mark in its etymology.
normalIntro.cn: 单音节短词；记忆抓手是酒馆的杯子与词源里画上去的记号。

normal.en: The medieval jar carried a painted mark — pint is the mark that measured the drink.
normal.cn: 中世纪的罐子上画着记号——pint 就是那道量酒的记号。

normal.en: In Britain, ask for a pint and beer arrives; in America, a pint may be ice cream.
normal.cn: 在英国说 a pint 端上来的啤酒；在美国可能是冰淇淋。

normal.en: Half a gallon makes a quart, two pints make a quart — the ladder of measures climbs by twos.
normal.cn: 两品脱成一夸脱——量制的梯子成倍往上爬。

normal.en: Pint-size teases a small person by measuring him in beer glasses.
normal.cn: pint-size 用啤酒杯给人量身高来打趣个子小。

normal.en: One syllable, five letters, one mark: the whole history of the measure is a painted line.
normal.cn: 一个音节、五个字母、一道记号：整个量制史就是一条画出的线。

abstract.en: Foam climbing over the rim of the pub glass, exactly to the painted line.
abstract.cn: 酒馆杯沿的泡沫正好爬到那道刻线。

abstract.en: A fridge shelf lined with identical pint cartons of milk.
abstract.cn: 冰箱架上排着一排一模一样的品脱牛奶盒。

abstract.en: The mark painted on a jug a thousand years ago still pours drinks tonight.
abstract.cn: 一千年前画在罐上的记号，今晚还在给人打酒。

examples.en: He ordered a pint of bitter and sat down slowly.
examples.cn: 他点了一品脱苦啤酒，慢慢坐下。

examples.en: Add half a pint of stock and let it simmer.
examples.cn: 加半品脱高汤，小火慢炖。

examples.en: The pint-size courier carried boxes bigger than himself.
examples.cn: 那个小个子快递员抱着比自己还大的箱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派恩特」——酒馆里特别给客人打满一杯，派恩特就是一品脱；pint 是量酒的。

root: pint 经古法语 pinte 追至通俗拉丁语重构形式 *pincta（pingere「画」的阴性过去分词），本义是画在量具上的记号；现代义为液量单位。

sensesIntro.en: One painted mark on a medieval jug became a standard measure, then the pub glass of beer, the milk carton and a joke about small size.
sensesIntro.cn: 中世纪陶罐上的一道记号变成标准量制，再变成酒馆的啤酒杯、牛奶盒和一个打趣个子的玩笑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a painted line on a jug that measures exactly one serving.
core.cn: 核心意象：陶罐上一道刻线，量出恰好一份。

branches.en: the official half-litre on paper
branches.cn: 纸面上的官方半升

branches.en: the foamy glass in the pub
branches.cn: 酒馆里冒泡沫的杯子

branches.en: the carton waiting in the fridge
branches.cn: 冰箱里等着的纸盒

branches.en: the teasing ruler for short people
branches.cn: 量小人用的玩笑尺

branches.en: from the statute book to the bar counter
branches.cn: 从法典到吧台

intro.en: Pint has no living prefix or suffix; its family is made of compounds and of measures that grew beside it.
intro.cn: pint 没有活的前后缀；它的词族由复合词和并肩生长的量制词构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb pingere, to paint, is the only classical element in the story, buried in the reconstructed form *pincta.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 pingere（画）是故事里唯一的古典成分，藏在重构形式 *pincta 里。

definition_zh: 强烈地；坚定地；坚固地
definition_en: in a powerful way, with firm feeling, or in a solid manner
core_image: 一只手重重拍在桌上，把话说得毫不含糊
scene: 我强烈建议你早点出发。 I strongly recommend that you leave early.
sceneCN: 这里 strongly 是「强烈地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我强烈建议你早点出发。

senses.title: With firm feeling
senses.definition: in a firm and powerful way, as of opinion
senses.definitionCN: 以坚定有力的方式，如表达看法
senses.example: I strongly recommend that you leave early.
senses.exampleCN: 我强烈建议你早点出发。
senses.why: This is force in a statement.
senses.whyCN: 这是话语里的力度。

senses.title: In a solid way
senses.definition: in a solid or powerful physical way
senses.definitionCN: 以坚固或有力的物理方式
senses.example: The house is strongly built.
senses.exampleCN: 这房子建得很坚固。
senses.why: The same force now shows in structure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的力量此时体现在结构上。

intro.en: Strongly is strong plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: strongly 由 strong 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Strang meant powerful.
items.cn: strang 意为强大的。

items.en: Strong kept the sense of force.
items.cn: 中古英语 strong 仍指力量。

items.en: Strongly described powerful action.
items.cn: strongly 描写有力的动作。

items.en: It came to mark firm opinions.
items.cn: 它开始标示坚定的看法。

items.en: It also described solid construction.
items.cn: 也用来形容坚固的建造。

note.en: Strongly is compared with look-alike words and with words for firmness.
note.cn: 把 strongly 与形近词以及表示坚定的词作比较。

entries.definition: having great power
entries.definitionCN: 强壮的

entries.definition: in a mistaken way
entries.definitionCN: 错误地

entries.definition: unusual
entries.definitionCN: 奇怪的

entries.definition: in a determined way
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地

entries.definition: very much
entries.definitionCN: 非常

entries.definition: with power
entries.definitionCN: 有力地

normalIntro.en: Strongly puts the weight of a strong word behind an action.
normalIntro.cn: strongly 把一个「强」字的重量压在动作后面。

normal.en: I strongly disagree with that.
normal.cn: 我强烈反对那一点。

normal.en: She is strongly influenced by her teacher.
normal.cn: 她深受老师影响。

normal.en: The bridge is strongly built.
normal.cn: 这座桥建得很坚固。

normal.en: He strongly believes in honesty.
normal.cn: 他坚信诚实。

normal.en: They strongly supported the plan.
normal.cn: 他们大力支持这个计划。

abstract.en: A strongly held belief can steady a shaking day.
abstract.cn: 一个坚定的信念，能稳住摇晃的一天。

abstract.en: To say strongly is to put your weight behind a word.
abstract.cn: 说得强烈，就是把你的分量压在话上。

abstract.en: Built strongly, a thing can outlast its builder.
abstract.cn: 建得坚固，东西能比建造者活得更久。

examples.en: I strongly recommend that you leave early.
examples.cn: 我强烈建议你早点出发。

examples.en: The house is strongly built.
examples.cn: 这房子建得很坚固。

examples.en: She strongly believes in honesty.
examples.cn: 她坚信诚实。

dict_mnemonic.text: strongly 是 strong 加 -ly；看法有力是强烈地，建造有力是坚固地，核心都是把「强」用在动作上。

root: 由 strong（强壮的、有力的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；strong 来自古英语 strang，因此 strongly 表示以强有力的方式，可用于意见、支持与建造。

sensesIntro.en: Strongly marks force in an opinion or solidity in a structure.
sensesIntro.cn: strongly 标示看法里的力度，或结构上的坚固。

core.en: A hand pressing a point home.
core.cn: 一只手把重点按实。

branches.en: A speaker repeats one clear word.
branches.cn: 发言者重复一个明确的词。

branches.en: A wall stands against the wind.
branches.cn: 一堵墙迎着风立着。

branches.en: A friend gives firm support.
branches.cn: 朋友给出坚定的支持。

branches.en: Strong words and strong walls both resist pressure.
branches.cn: 有力的话与坚固的墙，都抵得住压力。

branches.en: What is strongly made needs less repair.
branches.cn: 造得坚固的东西，需要修补得更少。

intro.en: Strongly is built from strong and adds no further endings.
intro.cn: strongly 由 strong 构成，本身不再加词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 我们强烈建议早点预订。
